name: en: Amaranthus (Dodo) Salad local_name: Saladi ya Dodo

name: en: Bbuga (Sautéed Pigweed/Amaranth) local_name: Bbuga
description: A simple, nutritious, and quick-to-prepare wild green, sautéed with basic aromatics. Bbuga has a mild, slightly earthy flavor and a tender texture when cooked, similar to spinach but often found growing wild.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly wash the bbuga leaves in several changes of water to remove all dirt, sand, and any small insects. Drain well in a colander. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_fresh_bbuga utensils: utn_colander
step_number: 2 instruction: Roughly chop the cleaned leaves if they are large. action: preparing_greens ingredients: ing_fresh_bbuga

step_number: 3 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onion utensils: utn_large_skillet_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: If using, add the chopped tomato and cook for 2-3 minutes until it begins to soften. action: cooking_base ingredients: ing_tomato
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the washed bbuga leaves to the pot. They will wilt down quickly. action: adding_greens ingredients: ing_fresh_bbuga
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the salt and 2 tablespoons of water. Stir everything together to combine. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt, ing_water

step_number: 7 instruction: Cover the pot and let it cook for 3-5 minutes over medium heat, until the leaves are completely wilted and tender. action: steaming cooking_indicators: visual: Leaves will turn a darker green and become soft. time: 3-5 minutes texture: Tender, similar to cooked spinach.
step_number: 8 instruction: Remove the lid and stir. If there is excess liquid, let it cook uncovered for another minute to evaporate. action: reducing
step_number: 9 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve immediately. action: finishing
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the bbuga hot as a side dish. action: serving

name: en: Bean Burger Patties local_name: Vifungu vya Burger vya Maharage
description: Hearty, flavorful, and protein-packed patties made from mashed beans, vegetables, and aromatic spices. They are pan-fried until golden brown and crispy on the outside, making a delicious and satisfying vegetarian burger or main course.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If using canned beans, drain and rinse them thoroughly. Place the cooked beans in a large mixing bowl and mash them with a potato masher or fork until mostly smooth but with some texture remaining. action: mashing_beans ingredients: ing_cooked_beans utensils: utn_large_mixing_bowl, utn_potato_masher_fork

step_number: 2 instruction: Add the finely chopped onion, minced garlic, diced bell pepper, breadcrumbs/oats, beaten egg, chopped herbs, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper to the mashed beans. action: combining_ingredients ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_bell_pepper, ing_breadcrumbs_oats, ing_egg, ing_fresh_cilantro_parsley, ing_ground_cumin, ing_paprika, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper

step_number: 3 instruction: Mix everything together until well combined. The mixture should be firm enough to hold its shape when formed into a patty. If it's too wet, add a little more breadcrumbs. If it's too dry, add a teaspoon of water or oil. action: mixing
step_number: 4 instruction: Divide the mixture into 6-8 equal portions. With damp hands, shape each portion into a round, flat patty about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick. action: shaping_patties

step_number: 5 instruction: Place the flour on a plate. Lightly coat each patty in flour, shaking off the excess. This helps create a nice crust when frying. action: coating ingredients: ing_flour utensils: utn_plate
step_number: 6 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_skillet

step_number: 7 instruction: Carefully place the patties in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Fry for 4-5 minutes on each side, until golden brown and crispy. action: frying cooking_indicators: visual: Deep golden brown and firm to the touch. time: 8-10 minutes total texture: Crispy exterior, firm and hot inside. utensils: utn_spatula
step_number: 8 instruction: Remove the patties from the skillet and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil. action: draining
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve the bean burger patties hot. action: serving

name: en: Boiled Beans local_name: Ebijanjaalo
description: A simple, nutritious, and comforting dish of beans slowly boiled until tender and creamy. This fundamental staple is a cornerstone of the Ugandan diet, providing affordable, plant-based protein to millions. The slow cooking process transforms hard beans into a soft, savory dish with a rich, creamy texture that perfectly complements other foods.
ingredients: Dry Beans (Nambale, Mwitemania, or Red Kidney Beans) (2)
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Sort through the dry beans carefully to remove any stones, debris, or damaged beans. Rinse thoroughly under cold running water. action: cleaning_beans ingredients: ing_dry_beans

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the cleaned beans in a large pot and cover with about 6 cups of water. The water should be about 2 inches above the beans. action: soaking_beans ingredients: ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 3 instruction: Optional: For faster cooking, you can soak the beans overnight or for at least 4 hours. Drain the soaking water before cooking. action: optional_soaking utensils: utn_colander

step_number: 4 instruction: If not soaking, add the pinch of cooking soda to help soften the beans. Add the chopped onion if using. action: adding_softening_agents ingredients: ing_cooking_soda, ing_onion
step_number: 5 instruction: Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer. action: bringing_to_boil

step_number: 6 instruction: Cover the pot and let the beans simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours. Check occasionally and add more hot water if needed to keep the beans covered. action: simmering cooking_indicators: time: 90-120 minutes olfactory: A warm, earthy, and comforting aroma will develop

step_number: 7 instruction: After about 1 hour, check the beans for tenderness. They should be soft but not mushy. Add salt only when the beans are almost tender, as adding it too early can harden them. action: testing_tenderness ingredients: ing_salt

step_number: 8 instruction: Continue cooking until the beans are very tender and the cooking liquid has thickened slightly to a creamy consistency. The beans should mash easily between your fingers. action: final_cooking cooking_indicators: texture: Beans are soft and creamy, with a thick cooking liquid
step_number: 9 instruction: If there is too much liquid, you can simmer uncovered for the last 10-15 minutes to reduce it to your desired consistency. action: adjusting_consistency
step_number: 10 instruction: Taste and adjust salt if needed. The beans should be savory and well-seasoned. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the boiled beans hot as a main dish or side. action: serving

name: en: Beans and Maize (Corn) Stew local_name: Kande / Kando
description: A hearty, wholesome, and nutritious one-pot stew of slow-cooked beans and maize (dried corn kernels), creating a complete protein and a foundational dish in Ugandan cuisine.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Drain the beans and maize that were soaked overnight. Rinse them thoroughly under cold running water. action: preparing ingredients: ing_beans, ing_maize utensils: utn_colander
step_number: 2 instruction: In a large, heavy pot, combine the rinsed beans and maize. Add 6 cups of water. action: combining ingredients: ing_beans, ing_maize, ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 3 instruction: Bring to a boil over high heat. Then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until both the beans and maize are tender. Skim off any foam that forms on the surface. action: boiling cooking_indicators: visual: The beans will split open slightly, and the maize will puff up and become soft. time: 60-90 minutes texture: Both beans and maize should be soft enough to eat easily.

step_number: 4 instruction: While the beans and maize are cooking, heat the vegetable oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onions until soft and translucent. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger (if using). Sauté for another 2 minutes until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 6 instruction: Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_curry_powder
step_number: 7 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes, mashing them with the spoon until they form a thick paste. action: cooking_base ingredients: ing_tomatoes

step_number: 8 instruction: Once the beans and maize are tender, pour this cooked tomato and onion mixture (the 'mchuzi') into the large pot with them. Add salt and stir everything together thoroughly. action: combining_stew ingredients: ing_salt

step_number: 9 instruction: Let the combined stew simmer uncovered for another 15-20 minutes over low heat. This allows the flavors to meld and the stew to thicken to your desired consistency. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. action: simmering cooking_indicators: visual: The stew will thicken and the colors will blend together. time: 15-20 minutes texture: Creamy and thick, with tender beans and maize.
step_number: 10 instruction: Taste and adjust the salt if needed. Serve hot. action: seasoning
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the Kande hot in a bowl. action: serving

name: en: Beef Pilau local_name: Pilau
description: A fragrant, spiced rice dish where beef is slow-cooked with a blend of Pilau Masala, then rice is added to absorb the rich, flavorful stock. Known for its distinctive brown color and aromatic depth.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Wash the rice thoroughly until the water runs clear. Soak it in water for 20-30 minutes, then drain completely. This helps achieve fluffier rice. action: preparing_rice ingredients: ing_basmati_rice utensils: utn_colander

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the thinly sliced onions and fry, stirring constantly, until they turn dark brown and crispy. This creates the 'birista' which gives the pilau its color and flavor. Remove half of the fried onions and set aside for garnish. action: frying_onions ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon

step_number: 3 instruction: To the remaining onions and oil in the pot, add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger

step_number: 4 instruction: Add the beef cubes and the roughly chopped onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the beef is browned on all sides. action: browning_meat ingredients: ing_beef, ing_onions

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the Pilau Masala and salt to the pot. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes to coat the beef and toast the spices. This is the most critical step for developing flavor. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_pilau_masala, ing_salt

step_number: 6 instruction: Pour in the hot beef stock or water. Add the bay leaves and the optional potatoes. name: en: Beef Luwombo with Mushrooms local_name: Luwombo lwa Nyama ne Butiko
description: A royal and aromatic Ugandan dish where tender beef and earthy mushrooms are slow-steamed to perfection in a rich, spiced sauce, all wrapped and cooked inside a banana leaf pouch. This method infuses the dish with a unique, smoky flavor and makes the meat incredibly tender.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft, glossy, and pliable. Cut into about 12x12 inch squares. action: preparing_leaves

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the beef cubes and brown on all sides. Remove and set aside. action: browning_beef ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_beef utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 3 instruction: In the same pot, reduce heat to medium. Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and golden brown. action: sautéing_onions ingredients: ing_onions
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. action: sautéing_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 5 instruction: Stir in the curry powder and smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds to toast the spices. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_curry_powder, ing_smoked_paprika

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the blended tomatoes and crumbled stock cube. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the mixture thickens and the oil begins to separate. action: making_sauce ingredients: ing_tomatoes, ing_beef_stock_cube

step_number: 7 instruction: Return the browned beef and any juices to the pot. Add the sliced mushrooms and salt. Stir well to combine and cook for 5 minutes. action: combining ingredients: ing_beef, ing_mushrooms, ing_salt
step_number: 8 instruction: Add the water, bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes, then remove from heat. This is your luwombo filling. action: finishing_filling ingredients: ing_water
step_number: 9 instruction: Place a prepared banana leaf square on a flat surface. Spoon a generous portion of the beef and mushroom filling into the center of the leaf. action: assembling

step_number: 10 instruction: Gather the edges of the banana leaf up around the filling to form a pouch. Tie the top securely with kitchen string. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling. action: wrapping utensils: utn_kitchen_string

step_number: 11 instruction: Place banana stems or a trivet at the bottom of a large, clean pot. Add about 2 cups of water, ensuring it doesn't reach the trivet. Carefully place the luwombo parcels on the trivet, seam-side up. Cover the pot tightly. action: steaming_setup utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_banana_stems

step_number: 12 instruction: Steam the luwombo over low-medium heat for 90 minutes. Check periodically and add more boiling water if needed to prevent the pot from drying out. action: steaming cooking_indicators: visual: Banana leaves will darken and become very fragrant. time: 90 minutes texture: Beef will be fall-apart tender and the sauce will be rich and thick.
step_number: 13 instruction: Carefully remove the parcels from the pot. Serve each luwombo pouch on a plate, allowing guests to open them at the table to release the aromatic steam. action: serving

name: en: Fried Bee Larvae (Gamanaani) local_name: Gamanaani
description: A seasonal, protein-rich delicacy consisting of bee larvae and pupae, lightly pan-fried until golden and crisp. They have a unique, nutty flavor and a creamy, slightly gritty texture, and are considered a great treat in many Ugandan communities.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Place the bee larvae in a colander and rinse gently under cold running water to remove any honey, wax, or debris. Be careful not to break them. Pat them dry gently with paper towels. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_fresh_bee_larvae utensils: utn_colander, utn_paper_towels
step_number: 2 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_skillet
step_number: 3 instruction: If using, add the sliced onion to the skillet and sauté for 2-3 minutes until it begins to soften. action: sautéing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 4 instruction: Carefully add the bee larvae to the hot skillet in a single layer. They may pop and sizzle. action: adding_larvae ingredients: ing_fresh_bee_larvae
step_number: 5 instruction: Sprinkle the salt and optional chili powder over the larvae. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt, ing_chili_powder

step_number: 6 instruction: Pan-fry the larvae for 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are uniformly golden brown, crisp on the outside, and have puffed up slightly. action: frying cooking_indicators: visual: Larvae turn golden brown and become crispy. time: 5-8 minutes texture: Crisp exterior, creamy interior. utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 7 instruction: Use a slotted spoon to remove the fried gamanaani from the skillet, allowing excess oil to drain. action: draining utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 8 instruction: Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb any remaining oil. action: cooling utensils: utn_paper_towels
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve the gamanaani immediately while hot and crispy. action: serving

name: en: Blood and Offals (Mala n'Ebikokiro) local_name: Mala n'Ebikokiro
description: A rich, deeply flavorful traditional dish that combines fresh animal blood with a variety of organ meats (offals) including liver, heart, kidneys, and tripe. This nutrient-dense preparation creates a complex texture and intense savory flavor that is highly valued in traditional cuisine. The blood forms a dark, thick sauce that coats the tender organ meats, resulting in a dish that is both hearty and packed with essential nutrients.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly clean all offals. Remove any membranes, fat, or blood vessels from the liver, heart, and kidneys. If using tripe, ensure it is well-scraped and cleaned. action: cleaning_offals ingredients: ing_liver, ing_heart, ing_kidneys, ing_tripe utensils: utn_knife
step_number: 2 instruction: Cut the heart into cubes, slice the kidneys, and cut the liver into bite-sized pieces. If using tripe, cut into strips. action: cutting_offals

step_number: 3 instruction: Strain the fresh blood through a fine strainer to remove any clots. Add vinegar or lemon juice and mix gently to stabilize. action: preparing_blood ingredients: ing_fresh_blood, ing_vinegar utensils: utn_strainer

step_number: 4 instruction: In a large pot, combine the heart, kidneys, and tripe (if using) with chopped onion, garlic, ginger, and salt. Add 4 cups of water. action: cooking_tough_offals ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt, ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot
step_number: 5 instruction: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30-40 minutes until the tougher offals are partially tender. action: simmering_tough_parts

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the liver and chopped chili peppers. Continue cooking for another 15-20 minutes until all offals are tender but not overcooked. action: adding_liver ingredients: ing_liver, ing_chili_peppers

step_number: 7 instruction: Reduce heat to very low. Slowly pour the prepared blood into the pot in a thin stream, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. action: adding_blood utensils: utn_wooden_spoon

step_number: 8 instruction: Stir gently as the blood begins to coagulate and cook. It will gradually thicken and turn dark brown, coating the offals. action: cooking_blood cooking_indicators: visual: The mixture will darken and thicken to a rich, dark sauce consistency
step_number: 9 instruction: Add the remaining 2 cups of water and continue to cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. action: final_cooking
step_number: 10 instruction: The dish is ready when the blood is fully cooked and has a firm but moist texture, and all offals are tender. Adjust seasoning if needed. action: testing_doneness
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve hot with your preferred staple food. action: serving

name: en: Boiled Blood with Meat (Mala) local_name: Mala
description: A rich, dark, and intensely flavorful traditional dish where fresh animal blood is carefully cooked with meat, creating a thick, savory, and nutritious stew. The blood coagulates during cooking, giving the dish a unique, firm texture and a deep, mineral-rich flavor that is highly valued in traditional cuisine. This is a dish of cultural significance, representing the utilization of every part of the animal.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If the blood has coagulated, strain it through a fine strainer to remove any lumps and achieve a smooth liquid consistency. action: preparing_blood ingredients: ing_fresh_blood utensils: utn_strainer

step_number: 2 instruction: Add the vinegar or lemon juice to the blood and whisk gently. This helps stabilize the blood and creates a better texture when cooked. action: stabilizing_blood ingredients: ing_vinegar utensils: utn_whisk

step_number: 3 instruction: In a heavy-bottomed pot, combine the meat chunks, chopped onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, and salt. action: combining_meat_aromatics ingredients: ing_meat, ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt utensils: utn_heavy_pot
step_number: 4 instruction: Add 3 cups of water to the pot, cover, and bring to a boil over medium heat. action: initial_boiling ingredients: ing_water

step_number: 5 instruction: Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until the meat is tender. action: simmering_meat cooking_indicators: texture: Meat should be tender but not falling apart

step_number: 6 instruction: Once the meat is tender, reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Slowly pour the prepared blood into the pot in a thin stream, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. action: adding_blood utensils: utn_wooden_spoon

step_number: 7 instruction: Continue to stir gently as the blood begins to coagulate and cook. It will gradually thicken and turn dark brown. action: cooking_blood cooking_indicators: visual: The mixture will darken and thicken to a pudding-like consistency
step_number: 8 instruction: Add the remaining 1 cup of water and chopped chili peppers. Stir gently to combine. action: adding_water_peppers ingredients: ing_chili_peppers

step_number: 9 instruction: Cover and let it cook on very low heat for another 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. action: final_cooking cooking_indicators: texture: The blood should be fully cooked and firm, but still moist

step_number: 3 instruction: Pour the 6 cups of water over the chicken and aromatics. The water should just cover the chicken pieces. action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water

step_number: 5 instruction: Cover the pot and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. action: bringing_to_boil

step_number: 6 instruction: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer. Cover and let it cook for 30-40 minutes. action: simmering cooking_indicators: olfactory: A pleasant smoky and savory aroma will develop. time: 30-40 minutes

description: A simple, healthy, and deeply satisfying dish where goat meat is boiled with basic aromatics until incredibly tender. Prepared without any oil, this method allows the natural, slightly gamey flavor of the goat to shine through, resulting in tender, flavorful meat and a rich, savory broth. instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Rinse the goat meat pieces under cold running water to remove any bone fragments or impurities. action: cleaning_meat ingredients: ing_goat_meat

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the goat meat chunks in a large pot. Add the quartered onion, crushed garlic, sliced ginger, salt, and whole chili peppers if using. action: combining_ingredients ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt, ing_chili_peppers utensils: utn_large_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Pour the 10 cups of water over the meat and aromatics. The water should completely cover the meat by at least an inch. action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water
step_number: 4 instruction: Cover the pot and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. action: bringing_to_boil

step_number: 5 instruction: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer. Cover and let it cook for 1.5 to 2 hours. action: simmering cooking_indicators: olfactory: A rich, meaty, and savory aroma will develop. time: 90-120 minutes

step_number: 6 instruction: If using green bananas (matoke), add the peeled bananas to the pot after the meat has been cooking for about 1 hour. They will cook in the flavorful broth and absorb the meaty flavors. action: adding_matoke ingredients: ing_green_bananas

step_number: 9 instruction: Reserve the rich, flavorful broth. It makes a nutritious soup or can be used as a base for cooking other dishes like rice or vegetables. action: reserving_broth
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the boiled goat meat hot with the matoke if used. action: serving

name: en: Plain Boiled Irish Potatoes local_name: obumonde
description: The simplest of preparations - fresh Irish potatoes boiled in nothing but water until tender. This method highlights the natural, earthy flavor and starchy goodness of the potatoes themselves. The result is soft, fluffy potatoes with a clean, comforting taste that serves as the perfect blank canvas for any meal.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Wash the potatoes thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or soil from the skins. You can scrub them with a brush if needed. action: cleaning_potatoes ingredients: ing_potatoes
step_number: 2 instruction: If desired, you can peel the potatoes. However, leaving the skins on is traditional and adds extra fiber and nutrients. action: optional_peeling utensils: utn_knife
step_number: 3 instruction: If the potatoes are large, you can cut them into halves or quarters to ensure even cooking. Small potatoes can be left whole. action: cutting_potatoes
step_number: 4 instruction: Place the prepared potatoes in a medium pot. action: pot_setup utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 5 instruction: Add enough cold water to completely cover the potatoes by about an inch (approximately 8 cups). action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water
step_number: 6 instruction: Cover the pot with a lid and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. action: bringing_to_boil

step_number: 7 instruction: Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium to maintain a gentle boil. Cover and cook for 15-25 minutes. action: boiling cooking_indicators: time: 5-10 minutes depending on potato size

step_number: 8 instruction: Test for doneness by piercing a potato piece with a knife or fork. It should slide in and out easily with little resistance. action: testing_doneness cooking_indicators: texture: The potatoes should be tender and fluffy throughout
step_number: 9 instruction: Once cooked, carefully drain the hot water using a colander. action: draining utensils: utn_colander

step_number: 10 instruction: Return the drained potatoes to the empty pot and place it back on the warm (but turned off) stove for a minute. This helps any residual moisture evaporate, making the potatoes fluffier. action: drying_potatoes
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the plain boiled potatoes immediately while hot. action: serving

instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Peel the potatoes and cut them into medium-sized chunks, about 2-inch pieces. Try to keep them uniform for even cooking. action: preparing_potatoes ingredients: ing_potatoes utensils: utn_knife

step_number: 3 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes to the pot. If not using oil, add the tomatoes and onions together with 1/4 cup of water and cook until softened. action: adding_tomatoes ingredients: ing_tomatoes
step_number: 4 instruction: Cook the tomatoes for 3-4 minutes until they begin to break down and form a light sauce. action: cooking_tomato_base
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the potato chunks to the pot and stir gently to coat them with the tomato-onion mixture. action: adding_potatoes

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the salt, curry powder (if using), and green pepper (if using). Pour in the 2 cups of water - it should come about halfway up the potatoes. action: adding_seasonings_water ingredients: ing_salt, ing_curry_powder, ing_green_pepper, ing_water

step_number: 7 instruction: Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes. action: simmering cooking_indicators: olfactory: A savory, comforting aroma will develop time: 20-25 minutes

name: en: Bongo (Fermented Milk) local_name: Bongo
description: A thick, tangy, and slightly effervescent fermented milk, traditionally prepared in long, dried gourds. Bongo is a staple for the Ankole, Banyoro, and Batooro people of Western Uganda. It has a complex, sour flavor profile, similar to a very strong, natural yogurt or kefir, and is valued for its refreshing qualities and long shelf life without refrigeration.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If using a traditional gourd (ekyano), ensure it is perfectly clean and dry. Traditional cleaning involves smoking the gourd over a fire and rinsing with special herbs. action: preparing_vessel

step_number: 2 instruction: If using raw milk, it can be used directly. If using pasteurized milk, allow it to cool to room temperature after boiling. action: preparing_milk ingredients: ing_fresh_milk
step_number: 3 instruction: Pour the fresh milk into the fermentation gourd or jar. action: transferring_milk

step_number: 4 instruction: Add the 2 tablespoons of existing Bongo (starter culture) to the fresh milk. This introduces the live bacteria necessary for fermentation. action: adding_starter ingredients: ing_starter_culture

step_number: 5 instruction: Close the gourd or jar with a loose-fitting lid or a plug of clean grass (oruhuura). Do not seal it airtight, as gases need to escape during fermentation. action: covering_vessel utensils: utn_grass_stopper

step_number: 6 instruction: Place the gourd in a warm, dark place, such as a kitchen corner or inside a granary, for 1 to 3 days. The fermentation time depends on the ambient temperature. action: fermenting cooking_indicators: time: 1-3 days olfactory: A clean, tangy, and slightly yeasty aroma will develop. visual: The milk will thicken and may separate slightly, with a clearer whey at the bottom.
step_number: 7 instruction: To check for doneness, gently shake the gourd. The contents should be thick and jiggle slightly. It should taste distinctly sour and tangy. action: testing_doneness
step_number: 8 instruction: Once fermented to your liking, the Bongo is ready to drink. It can be consumed immediately or stored in a cool place for several days. action: ready_to_serve
step_number: 9 instruction: To serve, the Bongo is often gently shaken or stirred and then poured directly from the gourd into a small serving calabash or cup. action: serving

name: en: white Rice local_name: Muceere Omususu
description: A wholesome, nutty-flavored whole grain rice where only the outermost inedible hull is removed, preserving the nutritious bran and germ layers. Brown rice has a chewy texture, earthy flavor, and significantly higher nutritional value compared to white rice. It cooks to a light, fluffy consistency with a distinctive nutty aroma and makes a perfect base for various Ugandan stews and sauces.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Place the white rice in a fine mesh strainer and rinse thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch and any debris. action: rinsing_rice ingredients: ing_white_rice utensils: utn_fine_mesh_strainer

step_number: 2 instruction: In a medium pot, combine the rinsed brown rice, water, salt, and oil (if using). action: combining_ingredients ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. action: bringing_to_boil
step_number: 4 instruction: Once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest setting and cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. action: reducing_heat

step_number: 5 instruction: Simmer gently for 35-40 minutes. Do not remove the lid during this time as the steam is essential for proper cooking. action: simmering cooking_indicators: time: 35-40 minutes olfactory: A nutty, earthy aroma will develop

step_number: 6 instruction: After 35 minutes, check if the rice is done. The water should be completely absorbed, and the rice should be tender but still slightly chewy. action: checking_doneness cooking_indicators: visual: Small steam holes will appear on the surface when done texture: Grains should be tender but still have a slight bite
step_number: 7 instruction: If the rice is not tender enough and there's no water left, add 2-3 tablespoons of hot water and continue cooking for 5 more minutes. action: adjusting_cooking
step_number: 8 instruction: Once cooked, remove from heat and let the rice stand covered for 5-10 minutes. This allows the grains to firm up and become fluffier. action: resting
step_number: 9 instruction: Fluff the rice gently with a fork or wooden spoon to separate the grains before serving. action: fluffing utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the brown rice hot as a nutritious staple. action: serving

name: en: Traditional Sand-Baked Cake local_name: Keki ya Mchanga
description: A unique and traditional method of baking where a cake batter is cooked in a pot buried in preheated sand, creating a gentle, even heat that results in a moist, perfectly baked cake with a distinctive aroma.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the sand by sifting it to remove stones and debris. Place the clean, dry sand in the large metal pot, filling it about halfway. action: preparing utensils: utn_large_metal_pot, utn_sand

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the pot of sand on the charcoal brazier or over the open fire. Heat the sand for 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is very hot. You should feel intense heat radiating from it. action: heating_sand utensils: utn_charcoal_brazier

step_number: 3 instruction: While the sand is heating, prepare the cake batter. In a mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy. action: mixing ingredients: ing_butter, ing_sugar utensils: utn_mixing_bowls
step_number: 4 instruction: Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract. action: mixing ingredients: ing_eggs, ing_vanilla
step_number: 5 instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. action: combining_dry ingredients: ing_flour, ing_baking_powder, ing_salt
step_number: 6 instruction: Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk, and mix until just combined. Do not overmix. action: combining ingredients: ing_milk

step_number: 7 instruction: Grease your cake tin or heatproof bowl. Pour the batter into the tin and cover the top tightly with aluminum foil or several layers of banana leaves to prevent sand from getting in. action: preparing_tin utensils: utn_cake_tin, utn_aluminum_foil
step_number: 8 instruction: Once the sand is hot, use a ladle or a smaller pot to remove about one-third of the sand from the center of the large pot, creating a well. action: creating_well
step_number: 9 instruction: Carefully place the covered cake tin into the well in the hot sand. action: burying

step_number: 10 instruction: Quickly and carefully shovel the hot sand back over the cake tin, completely burying it. Ensure the cake tin is surrounded by hot sand on all sides and on top. action: covering

step_number: 11 instruction: Cover the large pot with its lid. Place a few more hot coals on top of the lid to create an oven-like environment with heat from all sides. action: creating_oven utensils: utn_charcoal_brazier

step_number: 12 instruction: Bake for 45-60 minutes. Avoid opening the pot to check too soon, as this will release the heat. action: baking cooking_indicators: visual: After 45 min, carefully unearth and check. The cake is done when a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. time: 45-60 minutes texture: The cake will be golden, firm to the touch, and will have pulled away slightly from the sides of the tin.

step_number: 13 instruction: Once baked, carefully remove the cake tin from the sand using tongs or heatproof gloves. Let it cool for 10 minutes before turning it out onto a wire rack. action: cooling
step_number: 14 instruction: Allow the cake to cool completely before slicing and serving. action: serving

name: en: Chicken Fried Rice local_name: Muceere Oguterekwa Ogwa Nkoko
description: A hearty and flavorful one-pan meal where tender pieces of chicken are stir-fried with rice, colorful vegetables, and aromatic seasonings. This Ugandan-style chicken fried rice combines local ingredients with international techniques, resulting in a satisfying dish that's packed with protein and vegetables. The chicken adds savory depth while the vegetables provide crunch and nutrition.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Break up the cold cooked rice with your fingers to separate the grains and prevent clumping during frying. action: preparing_rice ingredients: ing_cooked_rice

step_number: 2 instruction: Cut chicken into small, bite-sized cubes. Season with chicken seasoning powder, salt, and black pepper. action: preparing_chicken ingredients: ing_chicken_breast, ing_chicken_seasoning, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper utensils: utn_knife, utn_cutting_board
step_number: 3 instruction: Beat the eggs in a small bowl with a pinch of salt. action: beating_eggs ingredients: ing_eggs utensils: utn_mixing_bowls, utn_whisk
step_number: 4 instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat. action: heating_oil_eggs ingredients: ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_large_wok
step_number: 5 instruction: Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside. action: cooking_eggs utensils: utn_spatula

step_number: 6 instruction: Add another tablespoon of oil to the same pan. Add the seasoned chicken and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Remove and set aside with the eggs. action: cooking_chicken
step_number: 7 instruction: Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil to the pan. Add chopped onion and sauté for 2 minutes until translucent. action: sauteing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 8 instruction: Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. action: adding_garlic ingredients: ing_garlic
step_number: 9 instruction: Add diced carrots and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened. action: cooking_carrots ingredients: ing_carrots

step_number: 10 instruction: Add green peas and diced green pepper. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until vegetables are tender but still crisp. action: adding_other_vegetables ingredients: ing_green_peas, ing_green_pepper
step_number: 11 instruction: Add the cooked rice to the pan. Stir well to combine with the vegetables. action: adding_rice

step_number: 12 instruction: Pour soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using) evenly over the rice. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until everything is well combined. action: adding_sauces ingredients: ing_soy_sauce, ing_oyster_sauce
step_number: 13 instruction: Add the cooked chicken and scrambled eggs back into the pan. Stir gently to distribute evenly. action: adding_chicken_eggs

step_number: 14 instruction: Continue stir-frying for 2-3 minutes until everything is heated through and the rice has a slightly crispy texture. action: final_stir_fry cooking_indicators: visual: Rice should be steaming hot with some crispy bits olfactory: Savory, chicken aroma will develop

step_number: 15 instruction: Drizzle with sesame oil and stir in most of the chopped spring onions, reserving some for garnish. action: finishing_touches ingredients: ing_sesame_oil, ing_spring_onions
step_number: 16 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The fried rice should be savory and well-balanced. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 17 instruction: Serve hot, garnished with the remaining spring onions. action: serving

name: en: Chicken in Groundnut Sauce local_name: Nkoko mu Binyebwa
description: A luxurious and deeply comforting stew where tender chicken pieces are simmered in a thick, creamy, and richly flavored sauce made from groundnut paste. The nutty, savory sauce perfectly complements the chicken, creating a hearty and satisfying dish that is a favorite for family meals and special occasions alike.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Heat the cooking oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces and brown them on all sides for about 5-7 minutes. You may need to do this in batches. Remove the chicken and set aside. action: browning_chicken ingredients: ing_cooking_oil, ing_chicken utensils: utn_heavy_pot
step_number: 2 instruction: In the same pot, reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sauteing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 3 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute to cook out its raw flavor. action: cooking_tomato_paste ingredients: ing_tomato_paste

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes, salt, and chicken seasoning. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and formed a thick sauce. action: making_tomato_base ingredients: ing_tomatoes, ing_salt, ing_chicken_seasoning

step_number: 6 instruction: Return the browned chicken pieces to the pot along with any accumulated juices. Add 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender. action: simmering_chicken ingredients: ing_water

step_number: 7 instruction: While the chicken is simmering, in a separate bowl, gradually whisk the groundnut paste with the remaining 2 cups of water until you have a very smooth, lump-free, creamy liquid. action: preparing_groundnut_sauce ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_whisk
step_number: 8 instruction: Once the chicken is tender, pour the smooth groundnut mixture into the pot. Stir gently to combine with the tomato base and chicken. action: adding_groundnut_sauce

step_number: 9 instruction: Bring the stew back to a gentle simmer. Oil may shimmer on the surface.
step_number: 10 instruction: Taste and adjust salt if needed. If the sauce is too thick, add a little hot water. Serve hot. action: final_seasoning_serving

name: en: Chicken Luwombo local_name: Luwombo y'Nkoko
description: A regal and aromatic dish where chicken is marinated with traditional spices, wrapped in banana leaves with a rich groundnut paste, and slowly steamed to perfection. The banana leaf pouch locks in all the moisture and flavors, resulting in incredibly tender, juicy chicken immersed in a thick, nutty, and deeply savory sauce. It is the pinnacle of Ugandan celebratory cooking.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the groundnut paste by grinding raw, shelled groundnuts with a small amount of water until a very smooth, thick paste forms. This can take 15-20 minutes by hand. action: making_groundnut_paste ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_grinding_stone

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with minced garlic, grated ginger, salt, and chicken seasoning powder. Mix thoroughly, ensuring the chicken is well-coated. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes. action: marinating_chicken ingredients: ing_chicken, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt, ing_chicken_seasoning utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 3 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft, glossy, and pliable. Be careful not to burn them. Wipe clean with a damp cloth. action: preparing_leaves

step_number: 4 instruction: Lay a softened banana leaf flat. Place a portion of the marinated chicken in the center. Top with sliced onion, tomato, a small piece of smoked meat/fish, and a generous spoonful of the raw groundnut paste. action: assembling_bundle ingredients: ing_onions, ing_tomatoes, ing_smoked_meat

step_number: 5 instruction: Fold the banana leaf over the filling to create a neat, sealed bundle. Tie it securely with kitchen string or a thin strip of banana leaf. Repeat for all portions. action: wrapping_bundles utensils: utn_kitchen_string

step_number: 6 instruction: Place a steaming rack or a bed of banana leaf stems at the bottom of a large pot. Add about an inch of water, ensuring it doesn't touch the rack. action: preparing_steaming_pot utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_steaming_rack
step_number: 7 instruction: Arrange the Luwombo bundles on the rack, seam-side up. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. action: loading_bundles

step_number: 8 instruction: Steam the bundles over medium-low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours. Check occasionally and add more boiling water if needed to prevent the pot from drying out. action: steaming cooking_indicators: olfactory: A rich, savory, and aromatic steam will escape when the lid is lifted. time: 1.5-2 hours

step_number: 9 instruction: Carefully remove one bundle to check for doneness. The chicken should be fall-off-the-bone tender, and the sauce should be thick and richly flavored. action: testing_doneness

step_number: 10 instruction: Once done, carefully remove the bundles from the pot. Serve each bundle on a plate, allowing diners to open their own pouch at the table to release the aromatic steam. action: serving

name: en: Cilantro Lime Rice local_name: Muceere Ogwa Cilantro n'Omudimu
description: A bright, fresh, and aromatic rice dish where fluffy white rice is infused with the zesty flavor of fresh lime and the herbal freshness of cilantro. The citrusy tang of lime perfectly balances the earthy rice, while the cilantro adds a burst of freshness that makes this dish incredibly refreshing and light. It's a perfect side dish that complements both Ugandan and international main courses.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Rinse the white rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well. action: rinsing_rice ingredients: ing_white_rice
step_number: 2 instruction: Zest one lime to get about 1 teaspoon of lime zest. Set aside. action: zesting_lime ingredients: ing_lime_zest utensils: utn_zester
step_number: 3 instruction: Juice all three limes to get about 1/4 to 1/3 cup of fresh lime juice. action: juicing_limes ingredients: ing_fresh_limes utensils: utn_juicer

step_number: 4 instruction: Finely chop the cilantro, including tender stems. You should have about 1 packed cup. action: chopping_cilantro ingredients: ing_fresh_cilantro utensils: utn_knife, utn_cutting_board

step_number: 5 instruction: Optional: For a more vibrant green color and smoother cilantro flavor, blend half of the cilantro with the lime juice in a food processor or blender. action: blending_cilantro_mixture utensils: utn_food_processor
step_number: 6 instruction: Heat cooking oil in a medium pot over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 7 instruction: Add chopped onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes until translucent. action: sauteing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 8 instruction: Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. action: adding_garlic ingredients: ing_garlic
step_number: 9 instruction: Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir to coat with oil. Toast for 1-2 minutes until the rice becomes slightly translucent around the edges. action: toasting_rice
step_number: 10 instruction: Pour in the stock or water and add salt. Bring to a boil. action: adding_liquid ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_chicken_vegetable_stock

step_number: 11 instruction: Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed. action: simmering_rice cooking_indicators: time: 15-18 minutes
step_number: 12 instruction: Remove from heat and let it stand covered for 5 minutes. action: resting

step_number: 13 instruction: Fluff the rice with a fork, then gently fold in the lime juice, lime zest, and chopped cilantro (or cilantro-lime mixture if blended). action: adding_flavors ingredients: ing_lime_zest
step_number: 14 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more lime juice or salt if needed. The rice should be bright and fresh-tasting. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 15 instruction: Serve immediately while the cilantro is fresh and vibrant. action: serving

name: en: Silver Fish in Cowpeas local_name: Mukene ne Bboojo
description: A savory, nutritious, and staple Ugandan dish that combines the intense umami flavor of dried silver fish with the soft, earthy texture of cowpeas, creating a protein-packed stew.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If using dried cowpeas, boil them in a separate pot in plenty of water for 45-60 minutes until tender. Drain and set aside. If using fresh cowpeas, they will cook with the stew. action: preparing ingredients: ing_cowpeas utensils: utn_large_saucepan, utn_colander

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the silver fish (mukene) in a bowl and rinse thoroughly under cold running water to remove sand, small stones, and excess salt. Drain well. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_silver_fish

step_number: 3 instruction: In a large saucepan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_saucepan, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the minced garlic and optional curry powder. Sauté for another minute until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_curry_powder

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes, mashing them with the spoon until they form a thick paste and the oil begins to separate. action: cooking ingredients: ing_tomatoes

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the rinsed silver fish to the pot. Stir well to coat with the tomato and onion mixture, and cook for 3-4 minutes to allow the fish to toast slightly and release its flavor. action: cooking ingredients: ing_silver_fish

step_number: 7 instruction: Add the pre-boiled (or fresh) cowpeas to the pot. Pour in the water and add salt cautiously (taste first). Stir everything to combine. action: combining ingredients: ing_cowpeas, ing_water, ing_salt

step_number: 8 instruction: Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes. step_number: 9 instruction: Once the cowpeas are tender and the stew has reached your desired consistency, remove from heat. Adjust seasoning if necessary. action: finishing
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve hot alongside a staple food like Posho (Ugali), Matoke, or Rice. action: serving

name: en: Deep-Fried Gonja (Plantain Chips) local_name: Gonja ya Kukaanga
description: Ripe plantains sliced and deep-fried until the edges are crispy and caramelized, while the inside remains soft and sweet. A simple, delicious, and addictive street food snack.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Peel the ripe plantains. Slice them diagonally into 1/2-inch (1-1.5 cm) thick pieces. Diagonally cutting creates a larger surface area for more crispiness. action: preparing ingredients: ing_ripe_plantains utensils: utn_knife

step_number: 2 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok over medium-high heat until hot (around 175°C / 350°F). The oil is ready when a small piece of plantain sizzles vigorously upon contact. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_deep_pot_skillet
step_number: 3 instruction: Carefully lower a batch of plantain slices into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot; fry in batches for even cooking. action: frying utensils: utn_slotted_spoon

step_number: 4 instruction: Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the gonja pieces are golden brown and the edges look dark and caramelized. action: frying cooking_indicators: visual: Golden brown with darker, crispy edges. time: 3-5 minutes per batch texture: Crispy exterior, soft and sweet interior.
step_number: 5 instruction: Use a slotted spoon to remove the deep-fried gonja from the oil, allowing excess oil to drip back into the pot. action: draining utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 6 instruction: Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels or a wire rack to drain and cool slightly. action: cooling utensils: utn_paper_towels
step_number: 7 instruction: While still warm, sprinkle with a little salt if desired. The contrast between the salty exterior and sweet interior is delightful. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt
step_number: 8 instruction: Serve the deep-fried gonja warm as a snack or side dish. action: serving

name: en: Dodo (Sautéed Amaranth Greens) local_name: Dodo
description: A simple, nutritious, and flavorful Ugandan staple made by sautéing amaranth greens with onions and tomatoes until tender. It has a unique, slightly earthy and peppery flavor and a soft, silky texture.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Wash the amaranth greens thoroughly in several changes of water to remove all grit and soil. Drain in a colander. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_amaranth_greens utensils: utn_colander
step_number: 2 instruction: Remove any tough stems and roughly chop the leaves. action: preparing_greens ingredients: ing_amaranth_greens

step_number: 3 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot or saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onion utensils: utn_large_pot_sufuria, utn_wooden_spoon

step_number: 4 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes, mashing them slightly with the spoon, until they soften and break down. action: cooking_base ingredients: ing_tomatoes
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the chopped dodo to the pot. It will seem like a lot at first, but it will wilt down significantly. action: adding_greens ingredients: ing_amaranth_greens
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the salt and 2 tablespoons of water. Stir everything together to combine the greens with the onion and tomato base. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt, ing_water

step_number: 7 instruction: Cover the pot and let it cook over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes. The greens will steam and release their own water. action: steaming cooking_indicators: visual: The greens will wilt completely and turn a dark green color. time: 5-7 minutes texture: The leaves should be very tender.

step_number: 8 instruction: Remove the lid and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, for another 2-3 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated. Be careful not to let it burn. action: reducing
step_number: 9 instruction: Taste and adjust the salt if needed. The dodo should be tender, flavorful, and not watery. action: finishing
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the dodo hot as a side dish. action: serving

step_number: 2 instruction: Heat cooking oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_heavy_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Add the sliced onions and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sauteing_onions ingredients: ing_onions
step_number: 4 instruction: Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 5 instruction: Add tomato paste and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw flavor. action: cooking_tomato_paste ingredients: ing_tomato_paste

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes, salt, fish seasoning, and chili pepper (if using). step_number: 7 instruction: Add the 1/2 cup of water and stir to create a thick sauce. action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water
step_number: 8 instruction: Gently place the marinated fish pieces into the sauce. Spoon some sauce over the fish to coat it. action: adding_fish ingredients: ing_fresh_fish

step_number: 9 instruction: Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes. Do not stir vigorously to avoid breaking the fish. Instead, gently shake the pan or spoon sauce over the fish. action: simmering_fish cooking_indicators: visual: The fish will turn opaque and the sauce will thicken significantly time: 15-20 minutes

step_number: 10 instruction: Remove the lid and continue cooking for another 5 minutes to allow any remaining liquid to evaporate, creating the 'dry' consistency. step_number: 11 instruction: The stew is ready when the fish is cooked through and flakes easily, and the sauce is thick and concentrated. Serve hot. action: testing_doneness

name: en: Eboo (Cowpea Leaves) local_name: Eboo
description: A traditional and highly nutritious dish made from the tender leaves of the cowpea plant. Eboo has a distinctive earthy, slightly bitter flavor and a mucilaginous (slightly slimy) texture when cooked, similar to okra. This texture is highly valued and helps to thicken the sauce, making it perfect for scooping with Ugali or Posho.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the eboo leaves by stripping the tender leaves from the tough stems. Wash them thoroughly in several changes of water to remove all dirt and grit. action: cleaning_and_prepping

step_number: 2 instruction: If using traditional soda ash (laro), dissolve the 1/2 teaspoon in 1 cup of water in the saucepan. action: dissolving_soda_ash ingredients: ing_soda_ash, ing_water utensils: utn_saucepan
step_number: 3 instruction: If NOT using soda ash, simply add 1 cup of plain water to the saucepan. Add the sliced onion and bring to a boil. action: boiling_water_base
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the washed eboo leaves to the boiling water. They will be voluminous but will quickly wilt down. action: adding_greens ingredients: ing_eboo_leaves

step_number: 5 instruction: Cover the pot and let the leaves boil for about 10-15 minutes until they are very tender and have developed a characteristic mucilaginous (slightly slimy) texture. action: boiling_greens cooking_indicators: visual: The leaves turn a dark green and the water becomes thick and slightly viscous. texture: The leaves should be very soft.

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the chopped tomato and salt. If using groundnut paste, mix it with a little water first to form a smooth paste, then stir it into the pot. action: adding_flavorings ingredients: ing_tomato, ing_salt, ing_groundnut_paste

step_number: 7 instruction: Stir everything together and continue to simmer uncovered for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken further. If it becomes too thick, add a little more water. action: simmering
step_number: 8 instruction: Taste and adjust the salt if needed. The dish should have a thick, cohesive sauce that coats the leaves. action: seasoning
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve the eboo hot as a flavorful and nutritious side dish. action: serving

name: en: Empogola (Smoked Matooke with Peelings) local_name: Empogola
description: A traditional and uniquely flavored dish from Western Uganda where whole, unpeeled green bananas (matooke) are smoked and steamed over a fire until the peel turns black and the inside becomes incredibly soft, sweet, and infused with a smoky aroma.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Build a steady fire using wood that produces a good amount of smoke (e.g., eucalyptus, coffee wood). Let the flames die down to a bed of hot embers and coals with consistent smoke. action: preparing_fire utensils: utn_open_fireplace

step_number: 2 instruction: Arrange the whole, unpeeled green bananas directly around the hot embers, ensuring they are close enough to cook but not so close that they burn instantly. They should be in the path of the smoke. action: arranging_matooke ingredients: ing_green_bananas utensils: utn_tongs

step_number: 3 instruction: Let the bananas smoke and cook for 60-90 minutes. Turn them every 15-20 minutes to ensure even cooking and smoking on all sides. action: smoking_cooking cooking_indicators: visual: The peel will become completely blackened, charred, and dry. The banana inside will feel soft when pressed. time: 60-90 minutes texture: The inner fruit is tender and steamed through.
step_number: 4 instruction: Remove the bananas from the fire using tongs and let them cool for a few minutes until they are safe to handle. action: cooling utensils: utn_tongs
step_number: 5 instruction: Once cool enough to handle, peel the bananas. The blackened skin should come off easily, revealing the soft, smoky, and creamy yellow flesh inside. action: peeling

step_number: 6 instruction: Place the peeled, smoked bananas on a clean, flat surface (traditionally a large, clean grinding stone) and mash them with the bottom of a clean bottle, a wooden pestle, or a large spoon until they form a smooth, cohesive mass. action: mashing utensils: utn_grating_stone_surface
step_number: 7 instruction: Shape the mashed matooke into a large, round mound on a serving platter. action: shaping
step_number: 8 instruction: Serve the Empogola immediately while still warm. action: serving

name: en: Garden Eggs Entula (Eggplant Stew) local_name: Entula ya Biringanya
description: A rich, creamy, and flavorful stew made from garden eggs (African eggplants) simmered in a savory groundnut (peanut) sauce. It has a unique, slightly bitter undertone balanced by the nutty, creamy sauce, creating a deeply comforting and nutritious dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Place the whole garden eggs and the roughly chopped onion in a large pot. Cover with water and boil for 15-20 minutes until the garden eggs are very tender and can be easily pierced with a fork. action: boiling_garden_eggs ingredients: ing_garden_eggs, ing_onions, ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 2 instruction: Drain the garden eggs, reserving about 2 cups of the boiling water. Let the garden eggs cool slightly, then peel off the skins (they should come off easily). action: peeling utensils: utn_mixing_bowl
step_number: 3 instruction: Return the peeled garden eggs to the pot. Use a masher or wooden spoon to mash them into a rough, chunky paste. action: mashing utensils: utn_masher

step_number: 4 instruction: In a separate bowl, mix the groundnut paste with 1-2 cups of the reserved boiling water (or fresh water) until you have a smooth, creamy, pourable consistency. action: preparing_groundnut_sauce ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 5 instruction: In a clean large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until soft and golden. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onions utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the tomato paste and curry powder. Stir and cook for 1 minute. action: cooking_paste ingredients: ing_tomato_paste, ing_curry_powder
step_number: 7 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 3-4 minutes until they break down. action: adding_tomatoes ingredients: ing_tomatoes

step_number: 8 instruction: Pour the groundnut sauce into the pot. Add the mashed garden eggs, the remaining salt, and the whole chili pepper. Stir well to combine. If using smoked fish or meat, add it now. action: combining_stew ingredients: ing_salt, ing_chili_pepper, ing_fish_meat

step_number: 9 instruction: Bring the stew to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and let it cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, until the stew has thickened and the oil starts to surface. action: simmering cooking_indicators: visual: The stew will thicken, darken in color, and oil will glisten on the surface. time: 15-20 minutes texture: Thick, creamy, and well-integrated.
step_number: 10 instruction: Adjust salt to taste. Remove the whole chili pepper if desired. Stir in fresh cilantro just before serving. action: finishing ingredients: ing_cilantro
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the Garden Eggs Entula hot in a bowl. action: serving

name: en: Essami (Pounded Cassava Leaves Stew) local_name: Essami
description: A rich, thick, and deeply flavorful stew from Northern Uganda made from finely pounded fresh cassava leaves, slow-cooked with groundnuts (peanuts), and often enriched with fish or meat. It has a distinctive dark green color and a unique, slightly bitter, earthy taste.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Wash the cassava leaves thoroughly in several changes of water to remove all dirt and sand. Drain. action: cleaning_leaves ingredients: ing_fresh_cassava_leaves

step_number: 2 instruction: Using a large mortar and pestle (or a blender in batches), pound/blend the cassava leaves until they become a fine, dark green paste. This is the most crucial and labor-intensive step. Add a very small amount of water if using a blender to facilitate the process. action: pounding_leaves ingredients: ing_fresh_cassava_leaves utensils: utn_mortar_pestle

step_number: 3 instruction: In a large, heavy pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_palm_oil, ing_onions utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down and soften. action: cooking_base ingredients: ing_tomatoes
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the pounded cassava leaves to the pot. Stir well to combine with the onion and tomato base. action: adding_leaves

step_number: 6 instruction: Dissolve the groundnut paste in about 2 cups of water to create a smooth, creamy liquid. Pour this into the pot with the leaves. action: adding_groundnuts ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water

step_number: 7 instruction: Add the remaining water, salt, the whole pierced chili pepper, and the optional potash or baking soda. Stir everything thoroughly. action: combining ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_chili_pepper, ing_soda_ash_potash

step_number: 8 instruction: Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to very low. Cover the pot and let it simmer gently for at least 1.5 to 2 hours. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking at the bottom. The long, slow cooking is essential for developing the flavor and tenderizing the leaves. action: slow_simmering cooking_indicators: visual: The stew will darken significantly, thicken to a paste-like consistency, and the oil will start to separate and rise to the top. time: 90-120 minutes texture: Very thick, smooth, and creamy.

step_number: 10 instruction: Once the stew has reached a thick, rich consistency and the raw taste of the leaves has completely cooked out, it is ready. Adjust salt to taste. action: finishing
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the Essami hot in a bowl. action: serving

name: en: Firinda with Beans and Ghee local_name: Firinda ya Maharage na Siagi
description: A rich, slow-baked casserole of tender beans cooked in a clay pot with ghee until creamy and deeply flavorful, creating a comforting one-pot dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Drain the beans that were soaked overnight and rinse them thoroughly under cold running water. action: preparing ingredients: ing_beans
step_number: 2 instruction: If using a traditional clay pot (firinda), soak it in water for 15-20 minutes to prevent cracking during cooking. action: preparing utensils: utn_clay_pot

step_number: 3 instruction: Melt 2 tablespoons of ghee in the clay pot or heavy oven-safe pot over medium heat. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_ghee, ing_onions utensils: utn_clay_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 5 instruction: Add turmeric and cumin powder. Stir for 30 seconds to toast the spices. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_turmeric, ing_cumin
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the grated tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides. action: cooking ingredients: ing_tomatoes
step_number: 7 instruction: Add the drained beans to the pot and stir well to coat with the tomato-spice mixture. action: combining ingredients: ing_beans
step_number: 8 instruction: Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. action: simmering ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt

step_number: 9 instruction: Cover the pot and let it simmer slowly for 2-3 hours. If using an oven, bake at 160°C (320°F) for the same duration. Stir occasionally and add more hot water if needed. action: slow_cooking cooking_indicators: visual: beans become very tender and creamy, sauce thickens time: 2-3 hours texture: beans should mash easily between fingers

step_number: 10 instruction: About 30 minutes before the end of cooking, stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons of ghee and diced green pepper (if using). This will enrich the flavor and aroma. action: finishing ingredients: ing_ghee, ing_green_pepper
step_number: 11 instruction: When the beans are completely tender and the sauce is thick and creamy, remove from heat. The beans should have a rich, buttery flavor from the ghee. action: finalizing

step_number: 13 instruction: Serve hot with Ugali, Chapati, or Rice, drizzled with extra ghee if desired. action: serving

name: en: Fish in Simsim Paste local_name: Emere y'Eyenyo mu Simsim

step_number: 3 instruction: Grind the toasted simsim seeds with about 1/2 cup of water until you get a smooth, thick paste. Traditional grinding stones work best, but a blender can be used. action: grinding_simsim_paste ingredients: ing_water utensils: utn_grinding_stone

step_number: 4 instruction: In a saucepan, sauté the chopped onion until translucent. Add garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant. action: sauteing_aromatics ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger utensils: utn_saucepan

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the chopped tomato, turmeric, and chili pepper (if using). Cook until the tomatoes break down and form a thick sauce, about 5-7 minutes. action: making_tomato_base ingredients: ing_tomato, ing_turmeric, ing_chili_pepper

step_number: 7 instruction: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly. action: simmering_sauce
step_number: 8 instruction: Gently place the marinated fish pieces into the simmering simsim sauce. Spoon some sauce over the fish to coat it completely. action: adding_fish

name: en: Cassava Leaves Stew local_name: Fresh Cassava Leaves
description: A traditional Ugandan-style stew made from fresh cassava leaves cooked until tender and enriched with groundnuts (peanut paste) or peanut butter, aromatics, and optional smoked fish or meat. Served with posho, rice, or matoke.
ingredients: fresh cassava leaves, washed and finely chopped (500 g)
peanut butter or groundnut paste (1/2 cup (smooth))
water or stock (2 cups (adjust as needed))
smoked fish or dried fish (optional) (100 g, flaked)
instructions: step: 1 instruction: Wash cassava leaves thoroughly. Remove tough stems and finely chop the leaves. If leaves are fibrous, pound lightly in a mortar or pulse briefly in a blender with a little water to help soften.
step: 2 instruction: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté chopped onion until translucent, then add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
step: 3 instruction: Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and form a loose sauce (4–6 minutes).

step: 4 instruction: Stir in the chopped/pounded cassava leaves. Add water or stock to cover and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 40–60 minutes until leaves are tender. Stir occasionally and add more water if needed.

step: 5 instruction: In a small bowl, mix the peanut butter with a little warm water to make a smooth paste. Add the groundnut paste to the pot and stir well to combine. Simmer another 10–15 minutes to thicken and allow flavors to meld.
step: 6 instruction: Add smoked fish or dried fish if using, and season with salt, black pepper, and chopped chili to taste. Adjust consistency with water or stock; cook 5 more minutes.
step: 7 instruction: Serve hot with posho, rice, matoke, or chapati. Garnish with a drizzle of oil or extra groundnuts if desired.

name: en: Goat Head Soup local_name: Mere Ow'Entama
description: A rich, gelatinous, and intensely flavorful soup made from a whole goat head, slow-simmered for hours with traditional herbs and spices. This delicacy is prized for its deep, savory broth, tender meat (especially the cheeks, tongue, and brain), and collagen-rich texture. It is a communal dish that showcases nose-to-tail eating at its finest.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly clean the goat head. Singe any remaining hair over an open flame, then scrub vigorously with a stiff brush and water. Pay special attention to the ears, nostrils, and mouth. action: cleaning_head ingredients: ing_goat_head utensils: utn_cleaning_brush
step_number: 2 instruction: Using a heavy knife or having the butcher do it, split the goat head in half or into manageable pieces to fit in the pot. action: splitting_head utensils: utn_knife
step_number: 3 instruction: Remove the brain and set aside (it will be added later). The tongue can be left in or removed and cleaned separately. action: removing_delicate_parts

step_number: 4 instruction: Place the goat head pieces in a very large stock pot. Add enough cold water to completely submerge the head (about 10 cups). action: pot_setup ingredients: ing_water utensils: utn_very_large_pot
step_number: 5 instruction: Bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Let it boil for 10-15 minutes, then skim off the scum that rises to the surface. action: initial_boil_skimming
step_number: 6 instruction: Drain the water and rinse the head pieces again. This first blanching ensures a cleaner, clearer broth. action: blanching_rinsing utensils: utn_strainer

step_number: 7 instruction: Return the cleaned head pieces to the pot. Cover with fresh cold water (about 10 cups again). Add the quartered onions, crushed garlic, sliced ginger, celery, carrots, salt, peppercorns, and chili peppers. action: adding_aromatics ingredients: ing_onions, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_celery, ing_carrots, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper, ing_chili_peppers

step_number: 8 instruction: Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting. Cover and let it simmer very gently for 3-4 hours. action: slow_simmering cooking_indicators: olfactory: A rich, meaty, and deeply savory aroma will develop. visual: The broth will become slightly milky and gelatinous.
step_number: 9 instruction: After about 3 hours, check for tenderness. The meat should be falling off the bone. Add the reserved brain in the last 20-30 minutes of cooking. action: adding_brain

step_number: 10 instruction: Once the meat is extremely tender, carefully remove the head pieces from the broth. Let them cool slightly until they can be handled. action: removing_meat utensils: utn_tongs

step_number: 11 instruction: Strain the broth through a fine-mesh strainer into a clean pot. Discard the solids. You should have a rich, flavorful, and slightly thick broth. action: straining_broth utensils: utn_strainer
step_number: 12 instruction: Pick all the meat from the goat head, including the cheeks, tongue, and any other tender parts. Return this meat to the strained broth. action: picking_meat
step_number: 13 instruction: Reheat the soup gently. Adjust seasoning with more salt if needed. The soup should be served very hot. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 14 instruction: Serve the soup in large bowls, ensuring each portion has plenty of meat and broth. action: serving

name: en: Goat Luwombo local_name: Luwombo y'Embuzi
description: A royal and exquisitely flavorful dish where marinated goat meat is steamed for hours inside a sealed banana leaf pouch. This ancient cooking technique locks in all the juices and aromas, resulting in fall-off-the-bone tender meat immersed in a rich, concentrated, and fragrant sauce. It is a dish of celebration, patience, and culinary artistry.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the groundnut paste by grinding raw, shelled groundnuts with a small amount of water until a very smooth, thick paste forms. This can take 15-20 minutes by hand. action: making_groundnut_paste ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_grinding_stone

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large bowl, combine the goat meat with the garlic-ginger paste and salt. Mix thoroughly and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes. action: marinating_meat ingredients: ing_goat_meat, ing_garlic_ginger, ing_salt utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 3 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft, glossy, and pliable. Wipe clean with a damp cloth. action: preparing_leaves

step_number: 4 instruction: Lay a softened banana leaf flat. Place a portion of the marinated goat meat in the center. Top with sliced onion, tomato, a piece of smoked meat/fish, and a generous spoonful of the raw groundnut paste. action: assembling_bundle ingredients: ing_onions, ing_tomatoes, ing_smoked_meat

step_number: 5 instruction: Fold the banana leaf over the filling to create a neat, sealed bundle. Tie it securely with kitchen string or a thin strip of banana leaf. Repeat for all portions. action: wrapping_bundles utensils: utn_kitchen_string

step_number: 6 instruction: Place a steaming rack or a bed of banana leaf stems at the bottom of a large pot. Add about an inch of water, ensuring it doesn't touch the rack. action: preparing_steaming_pot utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_steaming_rack
step_number: 7 instruction: Arrange the Luwombo bundles on the rack, seam-side up. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. action: loading_bundles

step_number: 8 instruction: Steam the bundles over medium-low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours. Check occasionally and add more boiling water if needed to prevent the pot from drying out. action: steaming cooking_indicators: olfactory: An incredibly rich, savory, and aromatic steam will escape when the lid is lifted. time: 2.5-3 hours

step_number: 9 instruction: Carefully remove one bundle to check for doneness. The meat should be extremely tender and pulling away from the bone, and the sauce should be thick and flavorful. action: testing_doneness

step_number: 10 instruction: Once done, carefully remove the bundles from the pot. Serve each bundle on a plate, allowing diners to open their own pouch at the table to release the aromatic steam. action: serving

name: en: Spiced Golden Rice local_name: Muceere Ogwa Turmeric
