instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Rinse the white rice thoroughly in a fine mesh strainer under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch. action: rinsing_rice ingredients: ing_white_rice utensils: utn_fine_mesh_strainer
step_number: 2 instruction: Heat cooking oil in a medium pot over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant. action: tempering_spices ingredients: ing_cumin_seeds
step_number: 4 instruction: Add chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sauteing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 5 instruction: Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_garlic ingredients: ing_garlic
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the turmeric powder and stir for 30 seconds to release its color and flavor. Be careful as turmeric can stain. action: adding_turmeric ingredients: ing_turmeric
step_number: 7 instruction: Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir gently to coat each grain with the spiced oil mixture. The rice will start to turn yellow. action: coating_rice

name: en: Grilled Chicken local_name: Nkoko eyokwooma
description: Succulent, flavorful chicken pieces marinated in a vibrant blend of onions, garlic, ginger, and citrus, then grilled over an open flame or charcoal. The result is juicy, tender meat with a beautifully charred, smoky, and crispy skin. A quintessential feature at social gatherings, roadside stalls, and backyard barbecues across Uganda.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: In a large bowl, combine the chopped onion, crushed garlic, grated ginger, lemon juice, cooking oil, salt, chicken seasoning, and chili powder (if using). Mix well to form a coarse marinade paste. action: making_marinade ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_lemon_juice, ing_cooking_oil, ing_salt, ing_chicken_seasoning, ing_chili_powder utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 2 instruction: Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Make 2-3 deep slashes on the thicker parts of each piece (like the breasts and thighs) to allow the marinade to penetrate. action: preparing_chicken ingredients: ing_chicken utensils: utn_knife

step_number: 3 instruction: Add the chicken pieces to the marinade bowl. Using your hands, rub the marinade thoroughly into the chicken, ensuring it gets into the slashes and under the skin where possible. action: marinating

step_number: 4 instruction: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight, for the most flavorful results. action: resting_marinade cooking_indicators: time: 2 hours to overnight

step_number: 5 instruction: Prepare your charcoal or gas grill for medium-high heat. The coals should be hot and covered with a layer of white ash. action: preparing_grill utensils: utn_charcoal_grill
step_number: 6 instruction: Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off. Reserve a little marinade for basting. action: ready_for_grill

step_number: 7 instruction: Place the chicken pieces on the grill, skin-side down first. Grill for 10-15 minutes until the skin is golden brown and has clear grill marks. action: grilling_first_side cooking_indicators: visual: Skin is crispy, browned, and releases easily from the grill.

step_number: 8 instruction: Flip the chicken pieces. Continue to grill for another 10-20 minutes, depending on the size of the pieces. Baste occasionally with the reserved marinade. action: grilling_second_side utensils: utn_tongs, utn_basting_brush

step_number: 9 instruction: The chicken is done when the juices run clear (not pink) when the thickest part is pierced with a knife or fork, and the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F). action: testing_doneness
step_number: 10 instruction: Transfer the grilled chicken to a clean platter, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. action: resting
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the grilled chicken hot with your favorite accompaniments. action: serving

name: en: Luwombo Groundnut Paste (Binyebwa for Luwombo) local_name: Binyebwa ya Luwombo
description: This is not a pourable sauce, but a thick, highly concentrated, and flavorful paste made from raw groundnuts. It is specifically used as a key ingredient in the ceremonial dish Luwombo. Spread over meat or mushrooms inside a banana leaf pouch, it steams and melts, creating an intensely nutty, rich, and aromatic gravy that infuses the entire dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If using raw groundnuts with red skins, you can remove the skins by rubbing them between your hands or blanching them briefly. This is optional but results in a smoother, more refined paste. action: preparing_nuts
step_number: 2 instruction: Using a grinding stone (or a food processor), begin grinding the raw groundnuts. They will first turn into a coarse powder. action: initial_grinding
step_number: 3 instruction: Continue grinding, adding a very small amount of water (a teaspoon at a time) to help the nuts release their oil and form a paste. action: adding_water_grinding

step_number: 4 instruction: Grind for a long time until the paste becomes very smooth, thick, and shiny, indicating the oils have been fully released. This can take 15-20 minutes by hand. action: achieving_smooth_paste cooking_indicators: texture: The paste should be thick, like natural peanut butter, and hold its shape.
step_number: 5 instruction: Transfer the smooth groundnut paste to a bowl. Mix in the grated onion and salt thoroughly. action: seasoning_paste

step_number: 6 instruction: The paste is now ready to be used. It should be thick enough to be spooned and spread over meat or other fillings in a banana leaf without being runny. action: ready_to_use
step_number: 7 instruction: The bowl is now placed on top of the food in banana leaves and wrapped with two or one banana leaf and left to cook. action: steaming_in_banana_leaf

name: en: Groundnut Sauce local_name: Binyebwa
description: A rich, creamy, and nutty sauce made from pure groundnut (peanut) paste. It is a versatile and beloved sauce that can be served with meats, vegetables, or simply poured over staples like Posho and Matoke. Its deep, savory flavor is a cornerstone of Ugandan cuisine.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: In a bowl, gradually mix the groundnut paste with about 1 cup of water, whisking until you have a smooth, lump-free, creamy liquid. action: dissolving_paste
step_number: 2 instruction: Pour the groundnut mixture into a saucepan. Add the remaining 2 cups of water, chopped onion, and tomato (if using). action: combining_in_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Place the saucepan over medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. action: simmering

step_number: 4 instruction: Once simmering, reduce the heat to low. Continue to cook, stirring often, for 15-20 minutes until the sauce thickens to a creamy, gravy-like consistency. action: thickening cooking_indicators: visual: The sauce will coat the back of a spoon and the oil may start to separate slightly on the surface. time: 15-20 minutes
step_number: 5 instruction: Stir in the salt. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. action: seasoning
step_number: 6 instruction: If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little more hot water to reach your desired consistency. action: adjusting_consistency
step_number: 7 instruction: Serve the hot groundnut sauce over your chosen dish. action: serving

name: en: Groundnuts with Mushroom Luwombo local_name: Luwombo lwa Ntuntunu ne Butiko
description: A rich and aromatic traditional Ugandan dish where a groundnut and mushroom stew is slow-steamed in a banana leaf pouch, infusing it with a unique smoky flavor.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft and glossy. This makes them pliable and prevents tearing. Cut into about 12x12 inch squares. action: preparing

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onions until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for another minute until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 4 instruction: Stir in the blended tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the oil begins to separate. action: cooking ingredients: ing_tomatoes

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the sliced mushrooms and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms begin to release their water. action: cooking ingredients: ing_mushrooms, ing_salt

step_number: 6 instruction: In a separate bowl, gradually mix the groundnut paste with water until you achieve a smooth, creamy, and pourable consistency. action: mixing ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 7 instruction: Pour the groundnut sauce into the pot with the mushroom mixture. Stir well to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes, then remove from heat. This is your luwombo filling. action: simmering
step_number: 8 instruction: Place a prepared banana leaf square on a flat surface. Spoon a generous portion of the groundnut and mushroom filling into the center of the leaf. action: assembling

step_number: 9 instruction: Gather the edges of the banana leaf up around the filling to form a pouch. Tie the top securely with kitchen string. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling. action: wrapping utensils: utn_kitchen_string

step_number: 10 instruction: Place banana stems or a trivet at the bottom of a large, clean pot. Add about 2 cups of water, ensuring it doesn't reach the trivet. Carefully place the luwombo parcels on the trivet, seam-side up. Cover the pot tightly. action: steaming_setup utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_banana_stems

step_number: 11 instruction: Steam the luwombo over low-medium heat for 60-90 minutes. Check periodically and add more boiling water if needed to prevent the pot from drying out. action: steaming cooking_indicators: visual: banana leaves will darken and become fragrant time: 60-90 minutes texture: sauce thickens and mushrooms become very tender
step_number: 12 instruction: Carefully remove the parcels from the pot. Serve each luwombo pouch on a plate, allowing guests to open them at the table to release the aromatic steam. action: serving

name: en: Boiled Fresh Groundnuts local_name: Binyebwa Eby'omumazzi
description: A simple, wholesome, and incredibly popular snack of fresh, immature groundnuts (peanuts) boiled in their shells with salt. The result is a uniquely soft, juicy, and savory nut with a texture and flavor entirely different from roasted peanuts. The act of cracking the warm, wet shells to get to the tender nuts inside is a quintessential Ugandan experience.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly wash the fresh groundnuts in their shells under running water, scrubbing them with your hands to remove any dirt and mud from the crevices. action: cleaning

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the cleaned groundnuts in a large pot. Add enough water to completely submerge them by at least an inch. action: pot_setup ingredients: ing_fresh_groundnuts, ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot

name: en: Honeyed Sweet Potato Balls local_name: Viazi Vitamu vya Asali
description: A delightful and wholesome snack or dessert made from mashed sweet potatoes, shaped into balls, and lightly pan-fried until golden, then rolled in a warm, aromatic honey glaze. A perfect blend of natural sweetness and comforting texture.

instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Place the peeled and cubed sweet potatoes in a pot and cover with water. Boil for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly. action: cooking_potatoes ingredients: ing_sweet_potatoes utensils: utn_pot

step_number: 2 instruction: Transfer the drained sweet potatoes to a mixing bowl and mash them until completely smooth. Allow to cool for 10-15 minutes. action: mashing utensils: utn_mixing_bowl, utn_masher

step_number: 3 instruction: Add the cornstarch (or flour), cinnamon, and salt to the cooled mashed sweet potato. Mix until a soft, workable dough forms. If it's too sticky, add a little more cornstarch. action: making_dough ingredients: ing_cornstarch_flour, ing_ground_cinnamon, ing_salt_ball
step_number: 4 instruction: With lightly oiled hands, take portions of the dough and roll them into smooth, bite-sized balls, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) in diameter. action: shaping

step_number: 5 instruction: Heat 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Place the sweet potato balls in the skillet, ensuring they don't touch. action: pan_frying ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil_frying utensils: utn_non_stick_skillet

step_number: 6 instruction: Pan-fry the balls for 5-7 minutes, turning them frequently with a spatula, until they are golden brown on all sides. action: cooking_balls cooking_indicators: visual: Golden brown and slightly firm on the outside time: 5-7 minutes texture: Crisp exterior, soft and hot inside utensils: utn_spatula
step_number: 7 instruction: Remove the balls from the skillet and set them aside on a plate. Reduce the heat to low. action: resting_balls

step_number: 8 instruction: In the same skillet, add the butter, honey, lemon juice, and water. Stir continuously for 1-2 minutes until the mixture is bubbly and has slightly thickened into a thin syrup. action: making_glaze ingredients: ing_honey, ing_butter_ghee, ing_lemon_juice, ing_water_glaze

step_number: 9 instruction: Return the fried sweet potato balls to the skillet. Gently toss and roll them in the honey glaze for about a minute until they are evenly coated and glossy. action: glazing

step_number: 10 instruction: Turn off the heat. Immediately transfer the honeyed sweet potato balls to a serving plate. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds while still sticky. action: garnishing_serving ingredients: ing_sesame_seeds utensils: utn_plate_tray
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the balls warm. action: serving

name: en: Obumonde in Rice (Savory Potato Rice) local_name: Obumonde mu Muceere
description: A comforting and flavorful one-pot dish that combines the savory goodness of Obumonde (sliced potatoes cooked with tomatoes and onions) with fluffy white rice. The potatoes and rice cook together, allowing the starches to meld and create a creamy, savory dish where each grain of rice is infused with the rich flavors of the potato-tomato mixture. It's the perfect fusion of two Ugandan staples into one satisfying meal.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain and set aside. action: rinsing_rice ingredients: ing_white_rice
step_number: 2 instruction: Peel the potatoes and slice them into thin rounds, about 1/4-inch thick. action: preparing_potatoes ingredients: ing_potatoes utensils: utn_knife
step_number: 3 instruction: Heat cooking oil in a medium pot over medium heat. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_cooking_oil utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 4 instruction: Add sliced onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sauteing_onion ingredients: ing_onion
step_number: 5 instruction: Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 6 instruction: Add tomato paste and curry powder. Stir for 30 seconds to cook out the raw flavor. action: cooking_tomato_paste ingredients: ing_tomato_paste, ing_curry_powder

step_number: 7 instruction: Add chopped tomatoes and green pepper (if using). Cook for 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes begin to break down. action: adding_tomatoes_pepper ingredients: ing_tomatoes, ing_green_pepper
step_number: 8 instruction: Add the sliced potatoes to the pot and stir to coat them with the tomato mixture. Cook for 2-3 minutes. action: adding_potatoes
step_number: 9 instruction: Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir gently to combine with the potato-tomato mixture. action: adding_rice
step_number: 10 instruction: Pour in the water and add salt. Stir gently to combine everything. action: adding_water_seasoning ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt

step_number: 11 instruction: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer for 15-18 minutes. action: simmering cooking_indicators: olfactory: A savory, comforting aroma will develop time: 15-18 minutes

step_number: 12 instruction: After 15 minutes, check if the rice and potatoes are cooked. The liquid should be absorbed, and both should be tender. action: checking_doneness cooking_indicators: texture: Rice should be fluffy and potatoes should be tender but not mushy
step_number: 13 instruction: If there's still too much liquid, simmer uncovered for 2-3 more minutes. If it's too dry, add 2-3 tablespoons of hot water. action: adjusting_consistency
step_number: 14 instruction: Remove from heat and let it stand covered for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. action: resting

step_number: 15 instruction: Fluff gently with a fork, being careful not to break the potato slices. Stir in most of the spring onions, reserving some for garnish. action: fluffing_garnishing ingredients: ing_spring_onions utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 16 instruction: Serve hot, garnished with the remaining spring onions. action: serving

description: Tender, buttery scones packed with sweet, tropical chunks of ripe jackfruit. These scones are lightly sweetened, with a fluffy interior and a slightly crisp exterior, making for a perfect breakfast or tea-time treat.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. action: preheating

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and granulated sugar. action: combining_dry_ingredients ingredients: ing_all_purpose_flour, ing_baking_powder, ing_salt, ing_granulated_sugar utensils: utn_large_mixing_bowl

step_number: 3 instruction: Add the cold, cubed butter to the flour mixture. step_number: 4 instruction: Gently fold the chopped jackfruit into the flour-butter mixture. action: adding_jackfruit ingredients: ing_ripe_jackfruit

step_number: 5 instruction: In a separate small bowl, whisk together the heavy cream (or coconut milk), egg, and vanilla extract. action: mixing_wet_ingredients ingredients: ing_heavy_cream, ing_egg, ing_vanilla_extract
step_number: 6 instruction: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Use a fork or spatula to gently stir until a shaggy dough just begins to form. Do not overmix. action: combining_wet_dry
step_number: 7 instruction: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently knead and pat it into a 7-inch (18 cm) circle, about 1-inch (2.5 cm) thick. action: shaping_dough
step_number: 8 instruction: Use a sharp knife or bench scraper to cut the circle into 8 equal wedges. action: cutting_scones utensils: utn_bench_scraper_knife

step_number: 9 instruction: Place the scones on the prepared baking sheet, about 2 inches apart. Brush the tops with milk or cream and sprinkle with coarse sugar if using. action: preparing_to_bake ingredients: ing_milk_cream_glaze, ing_coarse_sugar utensils: utn_baking_sheet, utn_brush

step_number: 10 instruction: Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the scones are golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. action: baking cooking_indicators: visual: Golden brown and well-risen. time: 18-22 minutes texture: A toothpick comes out clean.
step_number: 11 instruction: Allow the scones to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool further. action: cooling
step_number: 12 instruction: Serve the jackfruit scones warm or at room temperature. action: serving

name: en: Jobyo in Groundnut Sauce local_name: Jobyo mu Binyebwa
description: A hearty and flavorful stew where the distinct, slightly bitter taste of Jobyo (Acanthus) leaves is perfectly balanced by a thick, creamy, and nutty groundnut sauce. The robust greens hold their texture well in the rich sauce, creating a deeply satisfying and nutrient-dense dish that is a beloved comfort food in Northern Uganda.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a large pot. Add the pinch of baking soda and the chopped Jobyo leaves. action: pre_boiling_greens ingredients: ing_water, ing_baking_soda, ing_jobyo_leaves utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 2 instruction: Boil the Jobyo leaves for 5-7 minutes until tender and the initial bitterness is reduced. Drain the water and set the leaves aside. action: draining_greens cooking_indicators: visual: Leaves become a darker green and are soft to the touch.

step_number: 3 instruction: In the same pot, add the chopped onion and 1/2 cup of water. Cook over medium heat until the onion is soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. action: water_frying_onion ingredients: ing_onion, ing_water
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the chopped tomato and cook for another 5 minutes until it softens and breaks down into a sauce. action: cooking_tomatoes ingredients: ing_tomato

step_number: 5 instruction: In a separate bowl, gradually whisk the groundnut paste with 1.5 cups of water until you have a very smooth, lump-free, creamy liquid. action: dissolving_groundnut_paste ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_whisk
step_number: 6 instruction: Pour the smooth groundnut mixture into the pot with the tomato and onion base. Stir to combine. action: combining_sauce
step_number: 7 instruction: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Let it cook for 5-10 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent burning, until it thickens slightly. action: simmering_sauce
step_number: 8 instruction: Add the pre-boiled Jobyo leaves and salt to the pot. Stir well to coat the leaves in the sauce. action: adding_greens_to_sauce ingredients: ing_salt

step_number: 9 instruction: Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for another 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the Jobyo to fully absorb the nutty flavor. Stir occasionally. action: final_simmering cooking_indicators: texture: The sauce should be thick and creamy, coating the leaves thoroughly. The Jobyo should be tender but not mushy.
step_number: 10 instruction: If the stew is too thick, add a little more hot water to reach your desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt if needed. Serve hot. action: adjusting_serving

name: en: Kabalagala (Banana Pancakes) local_name: Kabalagala
description: Sweet, dense, and flavorful deep-fried pancakes made from a batter of mashed ripe bananas and flour. A classic Ugandan tea-time snack with a uniquely soft and cake-like interior and a crispy, golden-brown exterior.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Peel the very ripe bananas and place them in a mixing bowl. Mash them thoroughly with a fork or masher until you have a smooth paste with no large lumps. action: mashing_bananas ingredients: ing_ripe_bananas utensils: utn_mixing_bowl, utn_masher_fork
step_number: 2 instruction: Add the sugar, salt, and optional cardamom powder to the mashed bananas. Mix well. action: adding_flavor ingredients: ing_sugar, ing_salt, ing_cardamom

step_number: 3 instruction: Gradually add the flour to the banana mixture, stirring continuously to form a thick batter. The batter should be thick enough to hold its shape but still be droppable from a spoon. If it's too stiff, add a little water or milk, one tablespoon at a time. action: making_batter ingredients: ing_flour, ing_water_milk

step_number: 4 instruction: Heat the oil in a deep pot over medium heat until moderately hot (around 160-170°C / 320-340°F). The oil is ready when a small drop of batter sizzles and rises to the surface. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_oil utensils: utn_deep_pot
step_number: 5 instruction: Using a tablespoon, carefully drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot; fry in batches. action: frying utensils: utn_spoon

step_number: 6 instruction: Fry the kabalagala for 3-4 minutes on each side, turning once, until they are puffed up and a deep golden brown on all sides. action: frying cooking_indicators: visual: Deep golden brown and puffed up time: 6-8 minutes total per batch texture: Crispy exterior, soft and cooked through inside. utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 7 instruction: Use a slotted spoon to remove the kabalagala from the oil, allowing excess oil to drain back into the pot. action: draining utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 8 instruction: Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb any extra oil. action: cooling
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve the kabalagala warm or at room temperature. action: serving

name: en: Katogo - Matooke and Beans local_name: Katogo y'Matooke n'Ebijanjaalo
description: A hearty, comforting one-pot dish where green bananas (matooke) and beans are cooked together until tender, creating a thick, savory stew. The matooke absorbs the flavorful bean broth while becoming soft and creamy, resulting in a complete, nutritious meal that embodies Ugandan home cooking at its most comforting. This is the ultimate breakfast katogo that provides sustained energy throughout the day.
ingredients: Dry Beans (Nambale or Red Kidney Beans) (2)
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them thoroughly. Place them in a large pot with 4 cups of water. action: preparing_beans ingredients: ing_dry_beans, ing_water utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 2 instruction: Bring the beans to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45-60 minutes until they are partially tender but not fully cooked. action: cooking_beans cooking_indicators: texture: Beans should be soft but still hold their shape

step_number: 3 instruction: While beans are cooking, peel the matooke using plastic bags or banana leaves (traditional method) to protect your hands from staining. Cut into large chunks. action: peeling_matooke ingredients: ing_matooke utensils: utn_plastic_bags, utn_knife
step_number: 4 instruction: Keep the peeled matooke in salted water to prevent browning until ready to use. action: preserving_matooke

step_number: 5 instruction: In a separate small pan, heat cooking oil over medium heat. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. action: making_sauce_base ingredients: ing_cooking_oil, ing_onions
step_number: 6 instruction: Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 7 instruction: Add tomato paste and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw flavor. action: cooking_tomato_paste ingredients: ing_tomato_paste

step_number: 8 instruction: Add chopped tomatoes, curry powder, chili pepper (if using), and beef seasoning. Cook for 5-7 minutes until tomatoes break down and form a thick sauce. action: making_tomato_sauce ingredients: ing_tomatoes, ing_curry_powder, ing_chili_pepper, ing_beef_seasoning
step_number: 9 instruction: When beans are partially cooked, add the tomato sauce mixture to the beans in the large pot. Stir to combine. action: combining_beans_sauce
step_number: 10 instruction: Drain the matooke and add them to the pot, nestling them into the bean mixture. action: adding_matooke ingredients: ing_matooke
step_number: 11 instruction: Add salt and the remaining 2 cups of water. The liquid should come about halfway up the matooke. action: adding_water_seasoning ingredients: ing_salt, ing_water

step_number: 12 instruction: Cover the pot tightly and simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes. Do not stir vigorously - instead, gently shake the pot occasionally. action: slow_cooking cooking_indicators: olfactory: A rich, savory aroma will develop time: 45-60 minutes

step_number: 13 instruction: After 45 minutes, check for doneness. The matooke should be very tender and easily mashable, and the beans should be completely soft. action: testing_doneness cooking_indicators: texture: Matooke should be soft enough to mash with a fork

step_number: 14 instruction: Once cooked, gently mash some of the matooke into the bean sauce to thicken it. The katogo should have a thick, stew-like consistency. action: thickening_katogo utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 15 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The katogo should be savory and well-balanced. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 16 instruction: Serve hot in bowls, ensuring each portion has both matooke and beans with plenty of the flavorful sauce. action: serving

name: en: Lakotokoto (Acholi Groundnut & Simsim Paste) local_name: Lakotokoto
description: A rich, thick, and nutritious paste made from finely ground groundnuts (peanuts) and simsim (sesame seeds), traditionally served as a flavorful and energy-dense accompaniment to staple foods in Acholi culture.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: If using potash (achi), dissolve the small piece in 2 tablespoons of warm water and set aside. This will be strained and added later. action: preparing_potash ingredients: ing_achi

step_number: 2 instruction: Dry roast the raw groundnuts in a pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until they are lightly browned and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Remove and let cool. action: roasting_groundnuts ingredients: ing_raw_groundnuts utensils: utn_frying_pan

step_number: 3 instruction: In the same pan, dry roast the raw simsim seeds until they are golden and fragrant. Remove immediately and let cool. action: roasting_simsim ingredients: ing_raw_simsim utensils: utn_frying_pan

step_number: 4 instruction: Once cooled, rub the groundnuts between your hands to remove the skins. Winnow or blow to separate the skins from the nuts. action: peeling_groundnuts ingredients: ing_raw_groundnuts

step_number: 5 instruction: TRADITIONAL METHOD: Place the roasted, peeled groundnuts and roasted simsim on the grinding stone (atoke). Grind them together, adding a few drops of water occasionally, until they form a very smooth, thick, and oily paste. This requires significant time and effort. action: grinding_traditional utensils: utn_grinding_stone

step_number: 6 instruction: MODERN METHOD: Place the roasted, peeled groundnuts and roasted simsim in a high-powered blender or food processor. Blend on high, scraping down the sides frequently, until a smooth, buttery paste forms. You may need to add a tiny amount of oil (1 tsp) to help it blend if the nuts are not releasing enough oil. action: grinding_modern utensils: utn_modern_alternative

step_number: 7 instruction: In a heavy pot, bring the 3 cups of water to a gentle boil. If using the optional grated onion, add it now. action: heating_water ingredients: ing_water, ing_onion utensils: utn_heavy_pot

step_number: 8 instruction: Gradually add the groundnut-simsim paste to the boiling water, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps from forming. action: combining utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 9 instruction: If using the potash water, strain it to remove any solid bits and add the liquid to the pot. Add salt. action: adding_potash_salt ingredients: ing_achi, ing_salt

step_number: 10 instruction: Reduce the heat to very low. Let the Lakotokoto simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking at the bottom. It will thicken significantly as it cooks. action: simmering cooking_indicators: visual: The paste will thicken to a porridge-like consistency, and oil may start to separate and glisten on the surface. time: 15-20 minutes texture: Very thick and smooth.
step_number: 11 instruction: Once it has reached a thick, rich consistency, remove from heat. action: finishing
step_number: 12 instruction: Serve the Lakotokoto hot as a relish. action: serving

name: en: Fried Macaroni local_name: Macaroni ya Kukaanga
description: A quick, flavorful, and satisfying one-pan dish where cooked macaroni is stir-fried with vegetables and a savory sauce, creating a delicious meal that's a favorite for lunch or dinner.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Cook the macaroni according to package directions in a large pot of salted water until al dente (firm to the bite). Drain in a colander, rinse with cold water to stop the cooking, and set aside. action: cooking_pasta ingredients: ing_macaroni_pasta utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_colander

step_number: 2 instruction: While the pasta cooks, prepare all vegetables: chop the onion, mince the garlic, dice the bell pepper, grate the carrot, and chop the spring onions. action: prepping_vegetables

step_number: 3 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onion utensils: utn_large_wok_skillet, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the minced garlic and optional curry powder. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. action: cooking_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_curry_powder

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the diced bell pepper, grated carrot, and green peas. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp. action: cooking_vegetables ingredients: ing_bell_pepper, ing_carrot, ing_green_peas

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the cooked and drained macaroni to the wok. Pour the soy sauce and ketchup over the pasta. Season with salt and black pepper. action: combining ingredients: ing_macaroni_pasta, ing_soy_sauce, ing_tomato_ketchup, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper

step_number: 7 instruction: Toss everything together and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes, until the pasta is heated through and evenly coated with the sauce. action: stir_frying cooking_indicators: visual: Pasta is hot and has taken on the color of the sauce. time: 4-5 minutes texture: Pasta is tender, vegetables are crisp-tender.
step_number: 8 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. action: seasoning
step_number: 9 instruction: Remove from heat and stir in the chopped spring onions. action: garnishing ingredients: ing_spring_onions
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the fried macaroni hot immediately. action: serving

name: en: Mandazi (East African Doughnuts) local_name: Mandazi
description: Light, fluffy, and slightly sweet triangular doughnuts, popular throughout East Africa. They have a soft, cake-like interior and a golden-brown, lightly crisped exterior, often scented with cardamom or coconut.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water/milk, sugar, and instant yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until it becomes frothy. action: activating_yeast ingredients: ing_water_milk, ing_sugar, ing_yeast utensils: utn_large_mixing_bowl

step_number: 2 instruction: To the yeast mixture, add the melted butter/ghee, coconut milk, egg (if using), and cardamom powder. Whisk until well combined. action: combining_wet ingredients: ing_butter_ghee, ing_coconut_milk, ing_egg, ing_cardamom

step_number: 3 instruction: Gradually add the flour and salt to the wet ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms. action: adding_dry ingredients: ing_all_purpose_flour, ing_salt

step_number: 4 instruction: Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth, soft, and elastic. action: kneading cooking_indicators: visual: The dough is smooth and no longer sticky. time: 8-10 minutes texture: Soft and springy to the touch.

step_number: 5 instruction: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turn it to coat, and cover with a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size. action: first_proof cooking_indicators: visual: Dough has doubled in size. time: 60-90 minutes

step_number: 6 instruction: Punch down the risen dough to release the air. On a floured surface, roll it out into a large circle or rectangle about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick. action: shaping utensils: utn_rolling_pin

step_number: 7 instruction: Cut the dough into triangles, squares, or your desired shape. A pizza cutter works well for this. Traditionally, they are cut into triangles. action: cutting utensils: utn_knife_pizza_cutter

step_number: 8 instruction: Place the cut mandazi on a floured tray, cover with a cloth, and let them rest for 15-20 minutes for a second, shorter rise. action: second_proof cooking_indicators: visual: They will look slightly puffed up. time: 15-20 minutes

step_number: 9 instruction: Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat to 170-180°C (340-350°F). The oil is ready when a small piece of dough sizzles and rises to the surface immediately. action: heating_oil ingredients: ing_oil_frying utensils: utn_deep_fryer_pot

step_number: 10 instruction: Fry the mandazi in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes on each side, turning once, until they are puffed up and golden brown on both sides. action: frying cooking_indicators: visual: Golden brown on all sides time: 4-6 minutes total per batch texture: Puffed up and light utensils: utn_slotted_spoon
step_number: 11 instruction: Remove the mandazi with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towels to remove excess oil. action: draining
step_number: 12 instruction: Serve the mandazi warm. They are best enjoyed fresh on the day they are made. action: serving

name: en: Mashed Matooke and Liver Stew local_name: Matooke ne Bifuba by'Ente
description: A classic and beloved Ugandan comfort food pairing creamy, smooth mashed green bananas (matooke) with a rich, savory, and flavorful liver stew.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the liver: Place the sliced liver in a bowl. Add lemon juice or vinegar and a pinch of salt. Rub it thoroughly and rinse under cold water. This removes any bitterness and cleans it. Set aside. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_beef_liver, ing_lemon_juice, ing_salt utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 2 instruction: Peel the matooke. Use a knife to make a slit along the length of each finger and peel off the skin. Keep the peeled matooke in a bowl of water to prevent discoloration. action: preparing ingredients: ing_matooke

step_number: 3 instruction: Steam the matooke: Line a large pot with banana leaves (if using). Place the peeled matooke inside. Add a sliced onion on top for flavor. Add a small amount of water (about 1/2 cup). Cover tightly with more banana leaves and the pot lid. Steam for 30-40 minutes over medium heat until the matooke is very tender. action: steaming ingredients: ing_matooke, ing_onions utensils: utn_large_pot

step_number: 4 instruction: While the matooke is steaming, start the liver stew. In a saucepan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until soft and translucent. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_saucepan
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for one minute until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger

step_number: 6 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and curry powder. Cook for 5-7 minutes, mashing the tomatoes until they form a thick paste. action: cooking ingredients: ing_tomatoes, ing_curry_powder

step_number: 7 instruction: Add the cleaned liver slices to the pot. Stir well to coat with the sauce. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the liver changes color on all sides. action: cooking ingredients: ing_beef_liver

step_number: 8 instruction: Pour in one cup of water, add salt, and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat, cover, and let it cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the liver is cooked through and tender. Add the green pepper in the last 5 minutes of cooking. action: simmering ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_green_pepper cooking_indicators: visual: sauce thickens, liver is brown and cooked through time: 15-20 minutes texture: liver should be tender but not rubbery

step_number: 9 instruction: Mash the matooke: Once the steamed matooke is tender, transfer it to a separate bowl (or mash it directly in the pot). Use a wooden spoon or a masher to mash it until smooth and creamy. You can add a tablespoon of oil or a splash of hot water to achieve the desired consistency. action: mashing utensils: utn_masher
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the creamy mashed matooke hot, topped with a generous portion of the liver stew and its rich gravy. action: serving

name: en: Matooke Boiled in Kaveera (Black Polythene Bag) local_name: Matooke Eyokubikka mu Kaveera
description: A modern, convenient method of cooking matooke where peeled green bananas are tightly wrapped in a black polythene bag (kaveera) and boiled until tender. This technique steams the matooke in its own moisture, resulting in exceptionally soft, fluffy, and perfectly cooked bananas with a unique texture that many prefer over traditional methods. The kaveera acts as a steaming pouch that locks in flavor and nutrients.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Select firm, green matooke fingers. Avoid any with yellow spots or soft areas. action: selecting_matooke ingredients: ing_matooke
step_number: 2 instruction: Peel the matooke using a knife. You can use plastic bags on your hands to prevent staining if desired. action: peeling_matooke utensils: utn_knife

step_number: 3 instruction: Place the peeled matooke in a large, food-grade black polythene bag (kaveera). Arrange them neatly in a single layer if possible. action: placing_in_kaveera ingredients: ing_black_polythene_bag
step_number: 4 instruction: If using salt, sprinkle it over the matooke in the bag. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt

step_number: 5 instruction: Tie the top of the kaveera tightly with kitchen string or a rubber band, leaving some air inside to allow for expansion during cooking. action: sealing_kaveera utensils: utn_kitchen_string
step_number: 6 instruction: Place the tied kaveera in a large pot. action: placing_in_pot utensils: utn_large_pot
step_number: 7 instruction: Add enough water to completely cover the kaveera with at least 2 inches of water above it. action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water
step_number: 8 instruction: Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. action: bringing_to_boil

step_number: 9 instruction: Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and maintain a steady boil. Cook for 35-45 minutes. action: boiling cooking_indicators: time: 35-45 minutes visual: The kaveera will puff up with steam
step_number: 10 instruction: After 35 minutes, carefully remove the kaveera from the boiling water using tongs. Be cautious of the hot steam. action: removing_from_water utensils: utn_tongs
step_number: 11 instruction: Place the hot kaveera on a plate or in a bowl and carefully cut it open. Beware of the hot steam that will escape. action: opening_kaveera utensils: utn_knife

step_number: 12 instruction: Check the matooke for doneness. They should be very tender and easily mashable with a fork. action: testing_doneness cooking_indicators: texture: Matooke should be soft throughout and mash easily
step_number: 13 instruction: If not fully cooked, reseal the kaveera and return to boiling water for another 10-15 minutes. action: additional_cooking_if_needed
step_number: 14 instruction: Once cooked, transfer the matooke to a serving bowl. They will be very soft and may need careful handling. action: serving

name: en: Meat Luwombo local_name: Luwombo y'Nyama
description: A majestic and deeply flavorful dish where chunks of beef are slow-steamed for hours in a sealed banana leaf pouch with a rich groundnut paste and aromatic vegetables. This traditional cooking method transforms tough cuts of meat into incredibly tender, fall-apart morsels bathing in a thick, nutty, and intensely savory sauce. The banana leaf imparts a unique earthy aroma that defines this royal dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the groundnut paste by grinding raw, shelled groundnuts with a small amount of water until a very smooth, thick paste forms. This can take 15-20 minutes by hand. action: making_groundnut_paste ingredients: ing_groundnut_paste, ing_water utensils: utn_grinding_stone

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large bowl, combine the beef chunks with minced garlic, grated ginger, salt, and meat seasoning powder. Mix thoroughly, ensuring the meat is well-coated. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes. action: marinating_meat ingredients: ing_beef, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt, ing_meat_seasoning utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 3 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft, glossy, and pliable. Be careful not to burn them. Wipe clean with a damp cloth. action: preparing_leaves

step_number: 4 instruction: Lay a softened banana leaf flat. Place a portion of the marinated beef in the center. Top with sliced onion, tomato, a piece of smoked meat/fish, and a generous spoonful of the raw groundnut paste. action: assembling_bundle ingredients: ing_onions, ing_tomatoes, ing_smoked_meat

step_number: 5 instruction: Fold the banana leaf over the filling to create a neat, sealed bundle. Tie it securely with kitchen string or a thin strip of banana leaf. Repeat for all portions. action: wrapping_bundles utensils: utn_kitchen_string

step_number: 6 instruction: Place a steaming rack or a bed of banana leaf stems at the bottom of a large pot. Add about an inch of water, ensuring it doesn't touch the rack. action: preparing_steaming_pot utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_steaming_rack
step_number: 7 instruction: Arrange the Luwombo bundles on the rack, seam-side up. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. action: loading_bundles

step_number: 8 instruction: Steam the bundles over low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours. Check occasionally and add more boiling water if needed to prevent the pot from drying out. action: steaming cooking_indicators: olfactory: A deep, rich, and savory aroma will fill the kitchen. time: 2.5-3 hours

step_number: 9 instruction: Carefully remove one bundle to check for doneness. The meat should be extremely tender and easily pull apart with a fork, and the sauce should be thick and richly flavored. action: testing_doneness

step_number: 10 instruction: Once done, carefully remove the bundles from the pot. Serve each bundle on a plate, allowing diners to open their own pouch at the table to release the aromatic steam. action: serving

description: A classic, hearty one-pot dish where unripe green bananas (matoke) are steamed and cooked together with a flavorful beef stew. The matoke absorbs the rich, spiced broth from the meat, resulting in a tender, savory, and comforting meal.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Heat the cooking oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and translucent. action: sauteing
step_number: 2 instruction: Add the cubed beef and brown on all sides for about 5-7 minutes. action: browning_meat
step_number: 3 instruction: Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down and form a thick sauce, about 10 minutes. action: making_stew_base
step_number: 4 instruction: Add 1 cup of water, cover the pot, and let the beef simmer on low heat for about 45 minutes, or until the beef is tender. action: simmering_meat
step_number: 5 instruction: Drain the peeled matoke and add them to the pot, nestling them into the beef stew. action: adding_matoke

step_number: 6 instruction: Cover the pot tightly and let everything steam together on low heat for another 25-35 minutes, or until the matoke is very tender. Do not stir vigorously; gently shake the pot occasionally. action: steaming
step_number: 7 instruction: Once the matoke is soft and has absorbed the stew flavors, gently mash them slightly with the back of the spoon into the sauce. action: mashing
step_number: 8 instruction: Serve hot in a bowl, ensuring each portion has both matoke and beef stew. action: serving

name: en: Boiled Beef Hooves (Mlokony) local_name: Mlokony
description: A traditional Ugandan delicacy of beef hooves slow-boiled for many hours until the tough skin, tendons, and cartilage become incredibly soft, gelatinous, and tender. Served with a spicy, tangy dipping sauce.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly scrub the beef hooves under running water with a brush to remove any dirt or debris. Ensure they are split in half lengthwise. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_beef_hooves

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the cleaned hooves in the very large pot. Add the roughly chopped onion, crushed garlic cloves, sliced ginger, and salt. action: combining ingredients: ing_beef_hooves, ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_salt utensils: utn_very_large_pot
step_number: 3 instruction: Pour enough water into the pot to completely submerge the hooves. action: adding_water ingredients: ing_water

step_number: 4 instruction: Bring the pot to a rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting, cover the pot, and let it simmer very gently for 6-8 hours. action: slow_boiling cooking_indicators: visual: The water will become a rich, cloudy broth. The hooves will darken. time: 6-8 hours minimum texture: The meat, skin, and cartilage should be extremely tender and easily separate from the bone. A fork should pierce it with no resistance.
step_number: 5 instruction: Check the pot every hour or so, adding more boiling water if necessary to keep the hooves submerged. action: monitoring

step_number: 6 instruction: Once the hooves are completely tender, carefully remove them from the pot and place them on a large serving platter. They will be very soft and gelatinous. Reserve the nutrient-rich broth for drinking as a soup if desired. action: serving utensils: utn_serving_platter
step_number: 7 instruction: Serve the Mlokony hot or at room temperature. action: serving

name: en: Creamy Mushroom Sauce local_name: Mchuzi wa Uyoga
description: A rich, creamy, and deeply savory sauce made with fresh mushrooms sautéed with aromatics and simmered in a velvety broth and cream base. It's incredibly versatile and elevates any dish it accompanies.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Clean the mushrooms by wiping them with a damp cloth or brushing off any dirt. Slice them evenly. action: preparing_mushrooms ingredients: ing_fresh_mushrooms

step_number: 2 instruction: Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. The oil prevents the butter from burning. action: heating_fat ingredients: ing_butter, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_skillet

step_number: 3 instruction: Add the mushrooms to the hot skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes, without stirring too much initially, to allow them to brown and release their water. Once browned, stir and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated. action: browning_mushrooms ingredients: ing_fresh_mushrooms utensils: utn_wooden_spoon cooking_indicators: visual: Mushrooms will be golden brown and shrunken. time: 5-7 minutes

step_number: 4 instruction: Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Then add the minced garlic and fresh thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant. action: sautéing_aromatics ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_fresh_thyme

step_number: 5 instruction: If using wine, pour it into the skillet to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Let it simmer for 1-2 minutes until reduced by half. action: deglazing ingredients: ing_dry_white_wine

step_number: 6 instruction: Sprinkle the flour over the mushroom mixture and stir constantly for 1-2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste. This creates a roux that will thicken the sauce. action: making_roux ingredients: ing_all_purpose_flour
step_number: 7 instruction: Gradually pour in the stock while whisking continuously to prevent lumps from forming. action: adding_liquid ingredients: ing_beef_chicken_stock utensils: utn_whisk

step_number: 8 instruction: Bring the sauce to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Let it cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it has thickened nicely. action: simmering cooking_indicators: visual: Sauce will coat the back of a spoon. time: 5-7 minutes texture: Smooth and thickened

step_number: 9 instruction: Stir in the heavy cream (or coconut milk). Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let it heat through for 2-3 minutes, but do not boil after adding the cream. action: finishing_sauce ingredients: ing_heavy_cream, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper
step_number: 10 instruction: Remove the thyme sprigs. Stir in half of the fresh parsley. action: garnishing ingredients: ing_parsley
step_number: 11 instruction: Serve the mushroom sauce hot, garnished with the remaining parsley. action: serving

name: en: Nakati in Banana Leaves local_name: Nakati mu Bikoola
description: A traditional and flavorful preparation of Nakati (African eggplant leaves) where the vegetable is steamed inside a banana leaf pouch. This cooking method gently softens the nakati's characteristic bitterness while infusing it with a subtle, smoky-sweet aroma from the leaf, resulting in a uniquely tender and aromatic side dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Prepare the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame for a few seconds until they become soft, glossy, and pliable. Be careful not to burn them. Wipe clean with a damp cloth. action: preparing_leaves

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large bowl, combine the chopped nakati, sliced onion, chopped tomato, salt, and the 2 tablespoons of water. Mix thoroughly with your hands. action: mixing_ingredients ingredients: ing_nakati, ing_onion, ing_tomato, ing_salt, ing_water
step_number: 3 instruction: Lay a softened banana leaf flat. Place half of the nakati mixture in the center of the leaf. action: assembling_bundle

step_number: 4 instruction: Fold the banana leaf over the filling to create a neat, sealed bundle. Tie it securely with kitchen string or a thin strip of banana leaf. Repeat with the remaining leaf and nakati mixture. action: wrapping

step_number: 5 instruction: Place a steaming rack or a bed of banana leaf stems at the bottom of a large pot. Add about an inch of water, ensuring it doesn't touch the rack. action: preparing_pot utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_steaming_rack
step_number: 6 instruction: Arrange the nakati bundles on the rack, seam-side up. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. action: steaming_setup

step_number: 7 instruction: Steam the bundles over medium heat for 20-25 minutes. The nakati will cook in its own juices and the steam, becoming tender and absorbing the flavor of the leaf. action: steaming cooking_indicators: olfactory: A sweet, earthy, and vegetable aroma will emerge from the pot. time: 20-25 minutes
step_number: 8 instruction: Carefully remove the bundles from the pot. Let them rest for a minute before opening, as the steam inside will be very hot. action: resting
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve the nakati directly in the banana leaf bundles, allowing each person to open their own, or transfer the cooked vegetable to a serving bowl. action: serving

name: en: Traditional Offal Stew local_name: Malengu
description: A rich, deeply flavorful, and hearty stew made from a mix of cleaned tripe, intestines, and other organ meats, slow-cooked with aromatic spices until tender. A classic for those who appreciate bold flavors.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly clean the offal. Rub the tripe and intestines with lemon juice/vinegar and coarse salt. Rinse thoroughly under running water. Repeat until the water runs clear and the odor is minimized. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_tripe, ing_intestines, ing_lemon_juice, ing_salt utensils: utn_mixing_bowl

step_number: 2 instruction: Place the cleaned offal in a large pot. Add the sliced onion, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Boil vigorously for 10 minutes, then discard this water. This first boil further removes impurities. action: first_boil ingredients: ing_onions utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_colander

step_number: 3 instruction: Rinse the offal again and return it to the clean pot. Add fresh water until the offal is covered. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until the tripe is tender but still slightly chewy. Skim off any foam that rises. action: pre_cooking ingredients: ing_water cooking_indicators: visual: tripe becomes pale and tender, easily pierced with a fork time: 60-90 minutes texture: tender but with a bite
step_number: 4 instruction: Drain the pre-cooked offal and let it cool slightly. Cut it all into uniform, bite-sized pieces. Discard the boiling water. action: cutting utensils: utn_colander

step_number: 5 instruction: In the clean, large pot, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until golden brown. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_onions, ing_vegetable_oil utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 6 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger
step_number: 7 instruction: Stir in the curry powder and cumin powder. Cook for 30 seconds to release their aromas. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_curry_powder, ing_cumin_powder

step_number: 8 instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes, mashing them until they form a thick paste and the oil begins to separate. action: cooking_base ingredients: ing_tomatoes
step_number: 9 instruction: Add the pre-cooked offal pieces to the pot. Stir well to coat everything in the spiced tomato base. Cook for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. action: combining

step_number: 10 instruction: Pour in 4 cups of water, add salt, and add the whole chili pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until the stew has thickened and the offal is very tender. action: slow_simmering ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_chili_pepper cooking_indicators: visual: stew is rich and thickened, offal is very tender time: 45-60 minutes texture: offal should be melt-in-the-mouth tender
step_number: 11 instruction: Stir in the sliced green bell pepper in the last 10 minutes of cooking. Adjust salt and spice levels to your taste. action: finishing ingredients: ing_green_pepper
step_number: 12 instruction: Serve the hot offal stew in a deep bowl with its rich gravy. action: serving

name: en: Onion Rice local_name: Muceere Ogwa Tungurusumu
description: A simple yet deeply flavorful rice dish where onions are caramelized to sweet perfection and cooked with rice, allowing their rich, savory essence to infuse every grain. The slow-cooked onions transform ordinary rice into an aromatic, comforting dish that celebrates the humble onion's natural sweetness and complexity. This dish proves that sometimes the simplest ingredients create the most satisfying flavors.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Rinse the white rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well and set aside. action: rinsing_rice ingredients: ing_white_rice

step_number: 2 instruction: Peel the onions and slice them thinly into half-moons. Try to keep the slices uniform for even cooking. action: slicing_onions ingredients: ing_onions utensils: utn_knife, utn_cutting_board
step_number: 3 instruction: Heat cooking oil and butter (if using) in a medium pot over medium heat. action: heating_oil_butter ingredients: ing_cooking_oil, ing_butter utensils: utn_medium_pot
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the sliced onions to the pot. Stir to coat with oil and spread them evenly. action: adding_onions

step_number: 5 instruction: Cook the onions over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they become soft, golden brown, and caramelized. Be patient - this slow cooking develops the sweet flavor. action: caramelizing_onions cooking_indicators: visual: Onions will turn from white to golden brown to deep caramel color olfactory: Sweet, rich onion aroma will develop
step_number: 6 instruction: Add minced garlic to the caramelized onions and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. action: adding_garlic ingredients: ing_garlic

step_number: 7 instruction: Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir to coat each grain with the onion-infused oil. Cook for 2 minutes until the rice becomes slightly translucent around the edges. action: toasting_rice

step_number: 8 instruction: Pour in water or stock, then add salt, black pepper, and bay leaves (if using). Stir gently to combine. action: adding_liquid_seasoning ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper, ing_bay_leaves, ing_chicken_vegetable_stock

step_number: 9 instruction: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer for 15-18 minutes. action: simmering_rice cooking_indicators: time: 15-18 minutes
step_number: 10 instruction: After 15 minutes, check if the rice is cooked. The liquid should be absorbed, and the rice should be tender and fluffy. action: checking_doneness
step_number: 11 instruction: Remove from heat and let it stand covered for 5 minutes to allow the rice to steam and the flavors to meld. action: resting
step_number: 12 instruction: Remove the bay leaves if used. Fluff the rice gently with a fork, being careful not to break the grains. action: fluffing_rice utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 13 instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The rice should have a deep, sweet onion flavor throughout. action: final_seasoning
step_number: 14 instruction: Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley. action: serving ingredients: ing_fresh_parsley

description: A vibrant, sweet, and savory fried rice dish cooked with fresh pineapple, vegetables, and aromatic spices. This colorful one-pot meal is a delightful fusion of tropical flavors and a Ugandan staple.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Ensure your rice is cooked and completely cooled. Leftover rice from the previous day is ideal as it's drier and fries better without becoming mushy. action: preparing_rice ingredients: ing_rice

step_number: 2 instruction: Prepare all vegetables and pineapple: chop the onion, mince the garlic, dice the bell pepper and carrot, and cut the pineapple into small chunks. action: prepping_ingredients ingredients: ing_fresh_pineapple, ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_bell_pepper, ing_carrot utensils: utn_knife_cutting_board

step_number: 3 instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onion utensils: utn_large_wok_skillet, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 4 instruction: Add the minced garlic and sauté for another minute until fragrant. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_garlic
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the diced bell pepper and carrot. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften. action: cooking_vegetables ingredients: ing_bell_pepper, ing_carrot

step_number: 6 instruction: Push the vegetables to one side of the wok. Add the curry powder and turmeric to the empty space and toast for 30 seconds, then mix everything together. action: toasting_spices ingredients: ing_curry_powder, ing_turmeric

step_number: 7 instruction: Add the green peas and pineapple chunks. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until the pineapple is heated through and releases some of its juice. action: adding_fruit_veg ingredients: ing_green_peas, ing_fresh_pineapple

step_number: 8 instruction: Increase the heat to high. Add the cooled rice to the wok. Pour the soy sauce over the rice and add the salt and black pepper. Use the spoon to break up any clumps of rice. action: adding_rice ingredients: ing_rice, ing_soy_sauce, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper

step_number: 9 instruction: Stir-fry everything together for 4-5 minutes, tossing constantly, until the rice is evenly colored with the spices and heated through. action: stir_frying cooking_indicators: visual: Rice is hot and grains are separate, vegetables are tender-crisp time: 4-5 minutes texture: Fluffy and not mushy

name: en: Posho (Ugali) local_name: Posho
description: A thick, dense, and smooth porridge made from white maize flour (cornmeal) and water. It is the most common staple carbohydrate in Uganda, serving as the foundation for almost every meal, with a neutral taste that perfectly complements flavorful stews and sauces.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Bring the 4 cups of water to a rolling boil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add salt if using. action: boiling_water ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt utensils: utn_heavy_pot

step_number: 2 instruction: Reduce the heat to medium. Begin sprinkling the maize flour into the boiling water a little at a time, letting it sink before stirring. action: adding_flour ingredients: ing_maize_flour utensils: utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 3 instruction: As you add the flour, stir continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps from forming. This is the most critical step. action: stirring

step_number: 4 instruction: Once all the flour is incorporated, the mixture will be very thick and start to pull away from the sides of the pot. It will also form large bubbles that can pop and burn. action: cooking cooking_indicators: visual: The mixture becomes a thick, cohesive mass. time: 5-10 minutes after all flour is added

step_number: 5 instruction: Reduce the heat to low. Continue to stir and turn the posho, pressing it against the sides of the pot to cook out any raw flour taste and achieve a smooth texture. Cook for another 5-10 minutes. action: kneading_in_pot cooking_indicators: visual: The posho becomes firm and smooth. time: 5-10 minutes texture: Very thick, smooth, and holds its shape.
step_number: 6 instruction: Once the posho is smooth and no longer sticks to the sides of the pot, it is ready. It should be firm enough to hold a shape. action: testing_doneness
step_number: 7 instruction: Quickly transfer the hot posho to a serving bowl. Use a wet spoon to smooth the top into a round dome shape. action: shaping
step_number: 8 instruction: Serve the posho immediately while it is very hot and soft. action: serving

name: en: Crispy Potato Wedges local_name: Viazi vya Kukaanga
description: Potato wedges seasoned with aromatic spices and oven-baked or deep-fried until the outside is golden and crispy while the inside remains fluffy and tender. A universally loved snack or side dish.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). action: preheating

step_number: 2 instruction: Scrub the potatoes clean. You can peel them or leave the skin on for extra texture and nutrients. Cut each potato in half lengthwise, then cut each half into 3-4 wedges, depending on the size of the potato. action: cutting_wedges ingredients: ing_potatoes utensils: utn_knife_cutting_board

step_number: 3 instruction: Place the potato wedges in a large mixing bowl. Add the vegetable oil, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme/oregano, salt, black pepper, and optional cornstarch. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_paprika, ing_garlic_powder, ing_onion_powder, ing_dried_thyme_oregano, ing_salt, ing_black_pepper, ing_cornstarch utensils: utn_mixing_bowl
step_number: 4 instruction: Toss the wedges thoroughly until they are evenly coated with the oil and spice mixture. action: coating

step_number: 5 instruction: Arrange the wedges in a single layer on a large baking sheet, ensuring they are not touching. This allows them to crisp up instead of steam. action: arranging utensils: utn_baking_sheet

step_number: 6 instruction: Bake for 25-35 minutes, flipping the wedges halfway through, until they are golden brown, crispy on the outside, and tender on the inside. action: baking cooking_indicators: visual: Golden brown and crispy edges. time: 25-35 minutes texture: Crispy exterior, soft and fluffy interior.
step_number: 7 instruction: Remove from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes before serving. action: cooling
step_number: 8 instruction: Serve the potato wedges hot. action: serving

name: en: Grilled Cane Rat (Musu) local_name: Musu / Emmese
description: A traditional and highly prized game meat, where cane rats are carefully prepared, marinated with local spices, and grilled over charcoal until the skin is crispy and the meat is tender and flavorful.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Thoroughly clean the dressed cane rats. Rub them inside and out with lemon juice or vinegar and rinse well. This helps remove any gamey odor. Pat them dry with paper towels. action: cleaning ingredients: ing_dressed_cane_rat, ing_lemon_juice_vinegar utensils: utn_large_bowl
step_number: 2 instruction: Make several shallow cuts across the meat on both sides. This helps the marinade penetrate and allows for even cooking. action: scoring utensils: utn_sharp_knife

step_number: 3 instruction: Prepare the marinade by mixing grated onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped chili, vegetable oil, salt, and curry powder in a bowl. action: making_marinade ingredients: ing_onion, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_chili_pepper, ing_vegetable_oil, ing_salt, ing_curry_powder utensils: utn_large_bowl

step_number: 4 instruction: Rub the marinade mixture all over the cane rats, ensuring it gets into the cuts and the cavity. Cover and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes (or several hours in the refrigerator for deeper flavor). action: marinating
step_number: 5 instruction: Light the charcoal grill (sigiri) and let the flames die down until you have hot embers for a medium heat. action: preparing_grill utensils: utn_charcoal_grill
step_number: 6 instruction: Place the marinated cane rats on the grill rack or skewer them. Grill over medium-hot coals. action: grilling utensils: utn_grilling_skewers

step_number: 7 instruction: Grill for 20-30 minutes, turning frequently and basting occasionally with any remaining marinade or oil, until the meat is cooked through and the skin is crispy and charred in spots. action: cooking cooking_indicators: visual: The skin will be crispy and browned, and the meat will shrink from the bones. time: 20-30 minutes texture: Juices should run clear when the thickest part of the meat is pierced. utensils: utn_basting_brush
step_number: 8 instruction: Ensure the meat is fully cooked. The internal temperature should reach at least 75°C (165°F) if you have a meat thermometer. action: checking_doneness
step_number: 9 instruction: Remove the grilled musu from the heat and let it rest for a few minutes. action: resting
step_number: 10 instruction: Serve the grilled musu whole or chopped into pieces. action: serving

name: en: Raw Blood Mixture (Emyonyi/Ebinyebwa Omu Musaayi) local_name: Emyonyi/Ebinyebwa Omu Musaayi
description: A traditional, nutrient-dense preparation of fresh, raw animal blood mixed with partially digested stomach contents (from the same animal) and sometimes raw meat or fat. This ancient dish has a unique, strong flavor and creamy texture, and is consumed immediately after preparation for maximum nutritional benefit. It is considered a powerful source of vitality and strength.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Collect fresh, warm blood directly from the slaughtered animal into a clean gourd or bowl. Ensure the blood is from a healthy animal and collected hygienically. action: collecting_blood ingredients: ing_fresh_blood utensils: utn_clean_gourd

step_number: 2 instruction: Carefully extract partially digested stomach contents from the same animal's rumen. Strain if necessary to remove large, undigested plant matter. action: preparing_stomach_contents ingredients: ing_stomach_contents utensils: utn_strainer
step_number: 3 instruction: If using raw meat or fat, cut it into very small pieces using a sharp knife. action: preparing_meat ingredients: ing_raw_meat utensils: utn_sharp_knife
step_number: 4 instruction: Combine the fresh blood and stomach contents in the gourd or bowl. action: combining_base utensils: utn_clean_gourd
step_number: 5 instruction: Add the diced raw meat or fat if using. action: adding_meat
step_number: 6 instruction: Add salt if desired, though traditional versions may omit it. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_salt
step_number: 7 instruction: Mix thoroughly with a wooden paddle until well combined and smooth. The mixture should have a creamy, thick consistency. action: mixing utensils: utn_wooden_paddle
step_number: 8 instruction: The mixture is ready for immediate consumption. It should be consumed fresh, within minutes of preparation. action: ready_to_serve
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve directly from the gourd or transfer to individual drinking vessels. action: serving

name: en: Rice and Beans (One-Pot) local_name: Mchele na Maharage
description: A hearty, nutritious, and comforting one-pot dish where rice and beans are cooked together with aromatic spices, creating a complete protein and a staple meal found in households across Uganda.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Drain and rinse the beans that were soaked overnight. action: preparing_beans ingredients: ing_dried_beans utensils: utn_colander

step_number: 2 instruction: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. action: sautéing ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_onion utensils: utn_large_pot, utn_wooden_spoon
step_number: 3 instruction: Add the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for another minute until fragrant. action: cooking_aromatics ingredients: ing_garlic, ing_ginger

step_number: 5 instruction: Add the drained beans to the pot and stir to coat them in the tomato mixture. action: adding_beans ingredients: ing_dried_beans

step_number: 6 instruction: Pour in the 5 cups of water. Add the salt and the optional stock cube and whole chili pepper. Bring to a boil. action: adding_liquid ingredients: ing_water, ing_salt, ing_beef_chicken_stock, ing_scotch_bonnet

step_number: 7 instruction: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 30 minutes. This allows the beans to start becoming tender. action: simmering_beans cooking_indicators: visual: Beans will begin to soften but will not be fully cooked. time: 30 minutes
step_number: 8 instruction: Add the washed rice to the pot with the partially cooked beans. Stir gently to combine. action: adding_rice ingredients: ing_rice

step_number: 12 instruction: Serve the rice and beans hot. action: serving

name: en: Beef Stock Congee (Rice Porridge) local_name: Uji wa Mchele na Mtoro wa Nyama
description: A silky, smooth, and deeply savory rice porridge made by slow-simmering rice in a rich, homemade beef stock until it breaks down into a comforting, gruel-like consistency. Topped with seasoned beef and fresh aromatics.
instructions: step_number: 1 instruction: Make the beef stock: Place the beef bones in the large stockpot. Cover with 12 cups of cold water. Add the smashed ginger and garlic cloves, and the white parts of the spring onions. Bring to a boil. action: making_stock ingredients: ing_beef_bones, ing_water, ing_ginger, ing_garlic, ing_spring_onions utensils: utn_large_stockpot

step_number: 2 instruction: Once boiling, reduce heat to low, skim off any scum that rises to the surface. Cover and let it simmer gently for a minimum of 1 hour (2-3 hours is ideal for a richer stock). action: simmering_stock cooking_indicators: visual: The liquid will reduce slightly and become a rich, golden color. time: 60-180 minutes texture: Meat on the bones should be very tender.

step_number: 3 instruction: Strain the stock through a fine sieve into a clean pot. Reserve the tender meat from the bones, shred it, and set aside. Discard the bones and aromatics. action: straining_stock utensils: utn_fine_sieve

step_number: 4 instruction: You should have about 8-10 cups of rich beef stock. Return it to the clean pot. Add the washed, uncooked rice to the hot stock. (If using cooked rice, add it now). action: combining_rice_stock ingredients: ing_short_grain_rice

step_number: 5 instruction: Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting. Partially cover the pot and let it simmer very gently for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom. action: cooking_congee cooking_indicators: visual: The rice grains will burst and the mixture will thicken to a creamy, porridge-like consistency. time: 45-60 minutes texture: Silky smooth and thick.

step_number: 6 instruction: While the congee is cooking, prepare the beef topping. Heat vegetable oil in a small skillet. Sauté the minced garlic and julienned ginger for 30 seconds. Set aside. action: preparing_topping ingredients: ing_vegetable_oil, ing_garlic, ing_ginger, ing_soy_sauce utensils: utn_small_skillet
step_number: 7 instruction: Once the congee has reached your desired consistency, season it with the remaining soy sauce and salt to taste. action: seasoning ingredients: ing_soy_sauce, ing_salt

step_number: 8 instruction: Ladle the hot congee into bowls. Top with the seasoned beef, green parts of the spring onions, and fresh cilantro. action: assembling ingredients: ing_spring_onions, ing_cilantro
step_number: 9 instruction: Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top. action: serving ingredients: ing_lime
